title: Nice Shades, Great for Lazy People (Fewer Touch Ups)
text:
Yes, the packaging is gimmicky and I totally fell for it, but I make no apologies. I bought 3 shades--PK01, CR01, and OR01--and they're all quite nice. That said, the PK01 is a bit lighter than I expected so I'll probably get more wear out of the other two.

The tints are pretty long-lasting. I was able to wear the OR01 all day yesterday, and even through lunch and drinking mugs of tea I didn't need to touch it up 'til the end of the day. (And, truthfully, since it was the end of the day and there was still a hint of color, I was lazy and just didn't bother.) The tints aren't noticeably drying, either--although I'm a balm addict and usually put some on over the color throughout the day. Luckily, this doesn't seem to have a terribly detrimental effect on the color. There is a slight taste, which is neither unpleasant nor pleasant--I didn't especially like it, but it didn't bother me. I'm not a wine drinker, but my guess is they don't really taste like wine, just kind of fruity.

The only other true tints/stains I've used are the Tony Moly ones and I think these compare favorably to those in terms of ease of application (I think these are more forgiving), durability, drying, and taste (the TMs had a more chemical taste). I don't dislike the TM's, but these are just better, IMO.

I'd recommend these tints, and will probably buy again, especially to try out the other other colors.

title: Works Well on Dry, Cracked Heels
text:
I have for years dealt with dry, cracked heels, and I have tried a number of things to correct the issue. While my heels haven’t hurt or anything, they have been ugly. In a search for solutions, I found this foot scrubber and decided it was likely going to work better for me than a foot rasp, and I ordered it. It’s a great tool and it works well, though I do offer some caution for those who haven’t worked with a foot scrubber or rasp in the past.

This is an odd-looking instrument, vaguely similar to a comma in shape. The scraping side somewhat resembles a mirror with a patterned rough edge. It feels a lot like an emery board though it has more of a “bite” to the surface, if that makes sense. The overall size and shape make it easy to grip and hold, even when wet.

The first time I used it, I scraped away a fairly large amount of dead skin, to the point that I had feeling in parts of my heels where I have had no feeling for quite some time. It left my heels soft, pink and looking much better. However, I did discover that one can overdo, and I had nicked myself on each heel in one or two places, just enough to require blotting but not enough to really be a concern (it was less serious than a cut while shaving).

I discovered the following day what happens when you remove too much dead skin and don’t put enough lotion on an area that deals with weight and stress – my heels split in a couple of places and I ended up having difficulty walking without pain for a couple of days. I had put high-quality lotion on my heels, but apparently not enough. That was entirely my mistake, and it was a painful one.

After that finally healed up, I tried again. I have fallen into a daily routine where I gently scrub my heels for a couple of minutes each, then apply lotion. My heels now look much better, they’re not splitting when I put weight on them, and I have avoided nicking myself. At least in my case this is not a tool that gets used intensely every couple of weeks, but rather it is a daily tool that gets used very gently.

I got curious and put this tool under a digital microscope to see what the rough surface looked like. The roughness resembles a series of crescents, not dissimilar to a rasp, but much more fine.

This thing really works and it does a good job. It’s slightly more expensive than the average foot rasp but it seems to work well. I do recommend using some caution when working with this instrument as it is possible to overdo if not careful, which is probably very true of any tool of this type.

I am not very good at applying liquid liner, but I was able to get this liner to work just fine. I used these for my wedding and they stayed on all day/evening and weren't too heavy feeling like some lashes. They really made my eyes pop and stand out beautifully in pictures! In the photos, the close ups were before the wedding to try them out, and although the one end wouldn't stay on that time, I was able to get it to stay on the wedding day.

The only thing I didn't like (which is the same with all of these magnetic liners) is that the liner is difficult to remove. The lashes themselves came off fine, but the liner was not easy to remove (from my skin or the lashes). I don't like to use makeup removers, so I used coconut oil. It took some time to get it off. But I don't think that's anything specific to this liner, it's the magnetic liners in general.

I recommend these lashes over all of those 5 magnet ones!

title: Pricey, But Worth It To Have a GOOD Charger
text:
I own a Galaxy S6 Edge Plus... AND an iPhone 6 (Work Phone), AND a Galaxy Tab4 10.1, AND a New Trent Battery 12,000 mAh Pack. With that said, each one of these devices is using it's own charger and because of that, I had to resort using a power strip by my bedside JUST to charge all my devices.

The current chargers I use are all stock (1 Apple Charger, 3 Samsung Chargers). One of the Samsung Chargers is directly from the S6 Edge Plus (supports Adaptive Fast Charging/Quick Charge 2.0), yet it fails to work 80% of the time on my S6 Edge Plus for whatever reason...

Another issue is when I go away for overnight trips somewhere. For a day, I could probably just get by with just the iPhone charger & Samsung charger, but when I have 3-4 night stays due to work, I have to pack all of them!!! It's just a big hassle. That's when I decided I'm just going to resort to buying a GOOD multi-port charger. I've used Ankur devices in the past and I've been very pleased with all of them. After reading various reviews, I decided the 3-port is perfect for my situation.

For $25, you get a 3-port charger: 2 PowerIQ ports and 1 Quick Charge 2.0 port (which the Edge+ takes advantage of).

I've used the Ankur PowerIQ tech before via an Ankur Car Charger and I can definitely say it's almost as good as the Quick Charge 2.0 technology. What I like about it is that it supposedly "detects" what kind of device is connected to it and charges accordingly. Whether this is true or snake oil, I can say that it charges my devices fast and never has any kind of power dip when you have multiple devices connected to it. I use these two ports for my iPhone, Galaxy Tab4 and New Trent Battery pack.

The single Quick Charge is dedicated to my Galaxy S6 phone and right out of the box (same cables and all), it would fast charge my phone 100% of the time. Unlike my old stock Quick Charge Charger, it never seemed to work. So when I'm charging my phone and seeing it will fully charge within an hour makes me happy!

The only initial turnoff is the $25 sticker price. Yes you get a multi-port charger, but I think maybe that sticker price will scare some people. But after experiencing and using this product, I think that $25 is DEFINITELY WORTH IT. Never have a poor quality/flaky charger again. I'm 100% pleased with this item!

title: A Good Deal
text:
I bought these last year after I had purchased the cheap tv stamper set that was being sold at Sally's. Don't buy that set if you can help it. Get a Konad stamper and pick someone else's plates.

These Bundle plates, just like any other project/skill/product that you use have their drawbacks.
These plates do work well, and the newer sets come with a paper backing to protect the edges. Some people state that the images don't come through, but it really depends on a couple of things, so if your images don't come through on these plates, here are some things to keep in mind:
1. try a different stamper. I bought a Konad recently and it stamped beautifully, especially the delicate full-nail leaf pattern. Came out very well.
2. it could be your polish. Some of the wet and wild stuff works, china glaze does too, as does sally hansen. but it depends on the consistency and chemicals used in the polish, so don't be discouraged! I would recommend using the same brand of top coat that you are using to do the stamping design, because some I have used seem to "melt" the base coats away after a light brush.
3. it could be your technique. press firmly but evenly as you go down. Don't press hard enough to break your finger, but a little pressure may help in transfering. Also, work quickly, as the paint on the plate or stamped will dry.
4. it could be that you didn't clean the plate properly. I thoroughly clean out every desgin with acetone nail polish remover, and make sure all the cracks are clean. DO NOT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE USE NAIL POLISH REMOVER WITH MOISTURIZERS. THE OILS AND CHEMICALS MAY CAUSE THE NAIL POLISH NOT TO ADHERE TO THE STAMPER AND WON'T WORK!
5. the plate could be bad. I haven't tried every design, so I can't say which are bad, but they seemed to do okay. If you work fast and you roll the stamper in an even motion across your nails in one direction, and NOT back and forth, your design should be ok.
Overall, a good stamped makes a helluva lot of difference when doing this. Otherwise, they are good plates, although the rose doesn't come out too well in my opinion, and the full nail designs are too small, as many others have said. I'm not picky. I just match up and restamp the open space on the nail and it turns out good.
Overall, okay quality for the price and interesting designs for those who are just starting out and want to have something a little different to play with. Cheers!

title: Surprisingly Good
text:
I’m really glad I gave this one a second chance. I bought it, used it twice, decided I didn’t like the way it coated my face, and shoved it into a corner for about a month.
On a whim, I tried it again one day after a shower. What I noticed is that the light coating it provides made my moisturizer glide on like silk. As the day goes on, my face stays looking hydrated. So, I’ve been using it ever since for about two months. Now I feel like my routine would be incomplete without it.

You could, if you have oilier skin, use this as your only moisturizer in a pinch. I like that it primes my face so beautifully, even though I don’t wear makeup. It makes the moisturizer glide and settle nicely.

I *think* it also creates a sort of plump look to the skin. I am not sure that lessens scars or deals with discoloration yet. I do know, however, that it makes my skin look dewy and refreshed.

I’ve experienced no irritable or breakouts. My skin is hyper-sensitive, it reacts to fragrances even before they touch my skin. Sometimes it burns slightly upon application, but it does not irritate or damage the skin in any way.

It creates a very, very light coating on the face. But I have applied topical acne medication in spots over it and it didn’t prevent the treatment from penetrating. It plays well with niacinamide, which is in my la Roche Posay moisturizer, BP, and BHAs.

I wrote elta asking if I could apply it before applying my retinoid at night. They said they don’t know and told me to consult my derm. Therefore, I only use it in daytime, after my morning cleansing. I would like to try it as a buffer to my Tazorac at night, but until my derm says it’s okay, I won’t.

I think toners are absolutely necessary when you live in a hard water area like I do. But it has taken me years to find one that doesn’t break me out. Prior to this, I used rose water occasionally or no toner at all. I’m actually terrified elta will stop making this. Above all, its main benefit is that it removes residue from hard water and facial cleanser and restores the ph balance. That is all you should expect of a toner. But the added benefits listed above make this a keeper.

title: Battery wears out eventually
text:
I got this epilator about a year and a half ago and I've used it in average once a week on my legs, bikini area and armpits.

I like that it is wireless, so it gives you freedom to use it in different rooms and the cord does not get on the way. I also like that is a good size and easy to hold. I like that it has a light, although I normally use it on well lit areas, so it does not makes a big difference to me. The moving part is easy to clean (with the brush, included) and it can be washed with soap and water (I air dry it after that).

The epilator can only be used wireless, so if the battery is low and you haven't finished the job, you have to wait until it is fully charged again before being able to turn it on.

Mine takes about 30 minutes to fully charge and gives me about 45 mins of wireless use. However, a couple of weeks ago I noticed that even when it was fully charged, the red light (signaling low battery) started flashing after about 15 mins of use. I guess the battery wears out eventually, and as it cannot be used while it is plugged in, it will rend the whole epilator useless.

title: Very Good For Some Purposes, Difficult For Others
text: I have about 5 different colors of this Mofajang Hair Color Wax Temporary Hairstyle Cream, and I purchased them before I got this gray sample to try. what I like about these products is that they add a temporary color to my already light grey hair- such as a pink or purple tinge or even a darker gray or darker blue gray...you get the picture. This easily adds a pastel color to my lighter hair with a smallish amount of product.  I could see that to change up dark hair or to get a strong/intense color tone, you'd need to pile this stuff on, and I think that's where this gets a bad rap. Yes, you can glob this on to higher opacity and change your dark colored hair to the color shown in the jar. BUT, you need a lot to do this, and you may not like the sticky, waxy result -it is wax, after all. If you are using a little bit (about a quarter sized blob) and adding this through your washed and wet hair and then blow dry, your hair will still move naturally and have the lighter tone of the product, provided your hair was fairly light to begin with-- just my two cents.

title: A fantastic tool.
text:
This is a nice, heavy cleaver; really solid. It's almost a full 1/4" thick along the back of the blade, and the tang is full-width; the handle is all-metal, two shaped pieces of brass secured to the tang. The overall feel is very sturdy. The cleaver also has a hole for hanging.

This knife performs well for all kinds of cutting. Obviously it works well for heavy jobs like opening coconuts or hacking up meat still on the bone, but I was surprised at how well it does more delicate cuts, too. I was able to reduce a steak to thin slices for stir-fry very quickly -- the weight of this knife will carry it halfway through a cut on inertia alone, and then an easy slicing motion will finish the job, again with the weight of the blade doing the work.

Overall a great knife to add to even a small collection of kitchen tools, and an absolute steal at this price.

title: Observations
text:
As it turns out I live only 20 miles from West Coast Shaving. I called them and said I would drop in. While I was there I picked up a bunch of different blades, a new boar brush and Mitchells wool fat shaving soap. I've been wanting to try this stuff for a long time because of the reviews. The price varies depending on where you purchase it. I bought the refill only because it would fit perfectly in an empty shaving cream container I had. Next time I will buy it in the ceramic bowl. That may be a long time from now as this soap lasts forever.

Because everyone is different and must find the best combination of razor, brush, soap and blades I will not say that this is great and that over there is terrible. But I will make an observation. A new boar brush must be broken in which takes a couple of weeks because the tips of the bristles seem too firm and rather sharp when it's first used. My observation is that not only does the lanolin soften up your skin nicely but it has helped brake in the boar bruch very quickly. The lanolin seems to soften up the brush just like it softens up your beard. This only took about three shaves and my boar brush is perfect.

I read all the reviews and saw the videos on this soap. I didn't find any problems with the soap as far a lathering. I soaked it in WARM water and took my boar brush to start to lather it up. No problem. I didn't find all the problems that other people talk about. This might be the results of the water hardness rather than the soap itself.

title: 20 Year step backwards in closeness.
text:
#1) I bought this instead of the cheaper version because this had the Travel Case with it. What a JOKE. It's a wrap. My previous Norelco's all came with nice cases to travel with, but this is just some flimsy neoprene wrap... NOT worth the extra $20 or so that this cost over the basic model.

#2) I had the previous version of the CoolSkin razor, and really loved it. When the battery finally died in it, I purchases this one just because it was the next version of the razor I liked. This one, I can barely tolerate. Since I passed my "try it or money back" period, I'm stuck with this thing till I can find something better.

#3) This is obviously a razor that is put out just for it's funky look. Not how well it performs. The razor head covers keep falling off, all it takes is a slight twist and the head unit falls apart. The new head design is a single drive, instead of previous norelco units that drive all 3 heads independently. This razor is SLLLLOOOOWW! It reminds me of my first cordless razor from 1985! I wouldn't recommend using this in the shower, as you'll waste more money in water bills than getting a close shave outta this slow razor.

title: Who has good-looking brows?.. I do :)
text:
I will never go back to the salon to color my eyebrows again. This is exactly the same stuff the professionals use. The first time I did it I wasn't able to remove the product completely from my brows. I tried to make a home concoction to remove the dye. Boy, was that the worst thing to do. I only irritated my skin more by doing that. It looked funny for about 3 days and then I was beautiful again lol

The second time I did it I had the best experience. I used Dy-Zoff Hair Color Stain Remover Pads also from Amazon. I swear by these things. Two wipes and all the excess dye was removed.

Now as far as the dye goes which is what I want to focus on...you don't need to use a whole capsule. I poured about half of one and then closed it off for next time. That was enough for both my brows. The longer you leave the dye on the darker they get.

I'm blonde and I have really light brows. you can see about half of the brow without any added color. I like a darker brow look because I have darker roots and I think it really makes my blue eyes pop. I'll leave it on for about 4 minutes and then I'll do touchups after if I see areas should be a little darker. I recommend starting with one eyebrow at a time because it takes a while to apply the color. Don't be shy. Apply it heavy over the brow. you need to make sure all the hair is colored. My biggest mistake is I didn't bring the dye all the way to the ends so I had stray hairs that were left blonde. Not the biggest deal, but it bothered me a bit.

When you do this always start with less time then they say, just to be safe. It's always better to go lighter. You can always add color, but not take away. Have some dye remover (like the one I recommended) on hand, and do one brow at a time. The only reason why this gets 4 stars instead of 5 is because I experiences slight irritation after.

Good luck!

P.s. If I remember next time I do my brows I'll take a pic so you can see exactly what I mean.

I can’t stand to read a negative review on a great product simply because the reviewer didn’t use their head and fix the problem. Overall, this is by far a 5 star self tanner. Does this work as well as blotting sheeting (i.e. Clean and Clear wipes)? No. I'm not going to lie. It does NOT remove as much oil as the sheets do. BUT - it removes enough of it that I get rid of the vast majority of the shine, then just add some powder and voila! Oil free/shine free face.

Every damn pack of Clean and Clear wipes cost me 4-5 bucks, and I'd go through a pack in about two weeks. Not to mention, I was embarrassed to use blotting sheets in front of anyone else - at work, etc. - because it's just gross. I don't want everyone seeing the see-through splotch of oil that just came off my face. With this blotting sponge/compact, it just looks like I'm fixing up my makeup! No shame necessary.

title: Really like it - no more stubble, razor burn, or nicks
text:
Bottom line: This thing is great. It is a bit uncomfortable to use the first time, but it gets easier. If you can get a tattoo, you can easily use this thing.
What I'm glad it has: The exfoliation brush is really useful. It keeps me from getting ingrown hairs and makes my legs even smoother.
What I wish it had: It would be nice if there was a suction cup holder for the shower. If I use it in the shower, I have to turn off the water in order to put it on the floor outside the shower without flooding my bathroom.

I spent about two weeks researching epilators and reading hundreds of reviews and finally decided on the Braun Silk-epil 9. It has a big head, different attachments that are useful, and can be used wet or dry. I noticed that a lot of reviewers got it free, so I went to the BzzAgent site they reference, took some surveys, and thanks to my good karma, they sent me one to try out! Score! As soon as I got it, I scanned the instructions and held my breath as I held it up to my shin. I was worried it was going to be really painful, but it was just like a rubber band snap. It was a little uncomfortable, but not bad. As I got closer to my ankles, it hurt a little bit, but nothing too bad.

So, after successful use on my legs, I got cocky and decided to do my upper lip. I put on the other cap and brought it up to my upper lip. Oh mother of pearl! I couldn't do it. I've never waxed my lip and wasn't prepared for it. Not sure if you remember the first time you plucked your eyebrows, but it was a similar sensation. My eyes watered and I couldn't go through with it. I went online and did some research and saw that some people used lidocaine cream to numb the area. I tried that on my upper lip and bikini line and didn't feel a thing. I've been using the exfoliating brush and haven't had any ingrown hairs. I've use the epilator a few more times since and it's really not been bad at all.

One word of caution: If you have bug bites on your legs, be careful. I didn't realize that this little hair puller could also cut skin if it's swollen from a bug bite. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five.

Overall, I'm really happy with this epilator. I was completely prepared to buy it and, had I bought it instead of being awarded it, would have kept it. I have no desire to go back to shaving, razor burn, and nicks on my legs!

I have been trying to desensitize her since I've had her, and it just hasn't happened. I was nervous about the stability and safety of the harness, but my husband assisted in getting her hooked up, and I made sure I had everything I needed within reach before starting. I definitely would not hook your dog up too high off the ground, or leave him or her alone while in it. I know this sounds dramatic, but this product is life-changing! She was quiet as a mouse, totally still, and let me do everything she has fought me on from day one. I haven't shut up about this thing since using it. You have to keep an eye on how your dog's placement is doing as you go, and that they aren't getting wiggly or pulling their hind legs out. I also rigged up our system so that her front end was slightly higher than her back end - just a little, tiny, bit. This helped in keeping her stable and comfortable as well. If she were any heavier, I would not trust the clips or hooks included, and would purchase more sturdy hardware. However, for the price, it's definitely worth the sling alone. I also threw out the nail clippers because they got hung up in her fur around her nails, and they just weren't super quality. I am super happy with the purchase overall, and whoever thought this weird looking idea up? GENIUS.

title: I only use La Prairie  (this is the newest version of the name) products - for 12 years now!
text: Since there aren’t any reviews for this product, I thought I would write one for those who aren’t familiar with the brand, or the item. I’m now 66 years old and have been using only La Prairie products for my face since 2009/10. My face looks better than ever because of it. This item in particular is a very gentle, easy to apply and use, facial cleanser that doesn’t require any water or actual washing process. It goes on a cotton pad (not the balls!), and not too much either, and you gently wipe your face and eye lids going in a circular motion - and always apply outwards and upwards. This will help your skin from being pulled down, which can cause more wrinkles. The company has changed the exact name of the product, but it’s the same (only an improved version) as it always has been. For me, I use this as the first step in my nightly facial ritual - which is to cleanse the face. I follow with other products in stages, finishing up with the moisturizer (one for the face and a different one for the eyes). My rating of this being sold online is hard, since it’s a wonderful product, however it’s outrageously overpriced for what’s a ‘trial size’ and ‘free’ gift, given out with purchases of a full size La Prairie item (depending on how much you spend, and where you buy, it might be just one of multiple free trial size items). The FULL size of this item is about $100 USD, and it’s around 8 ounces +/-. The bottle is probably 8” high and a couple inches wide at least. So part of my rating is based on the product itself and the other part is on the price for this size. Another thing I want to mention is that I have sensitive skin and have never had any issues with this product line! You’re face will thank you!

title: These are not USDA certified oils. 2 stars ✨
text:
First, I will say these oils seem fine. They work well together or apart, mixed into other skincare products or alone. I use these types of oils to make my own facial oil mix or to add to my moisturizer.
The thing I absolutely hate that companies do to try to sell their products is to say things that aren't true. The USDA does not certify oils - food, cosmetic, or otherwise. The fact that the bottle says this product is USDA certified on one side, and the other side says not intended for ingestion should speak volumes. The USDA certifies and regulates the welfare and production of food products; meaning products that you ingest. So, why on earth would they certify a product you cannot ingest? The bottle also makes outright claims of known cures from using these oils. There is no disclaimer on either bottle that states that these claims have not been approved or proven by the FDA, or whatever the disclaimer is that is mandatory. There are ingredients listed, one ingredient for each product, the oil, and that's it. Nothing tells how these oils were extracted. Therefore, we do not know if they are refined or unrefined. They probably don't know either. So you see, therein lies the lies and deception.
These oils would be much better if they weren't tied to lies. Because you know what they say about lies... if you tell one you have to tell more to keep up with the first one. Is what they say in the bottle really what's in the bottle? Are they pure oils or mixed with a lesser oil? Oils are greasy. If they are unrefined, why aren't they greasy? When you refine oils, you take away a lot of their natural properties and their nutritive value, is that why they aren't greasy? Because of the lies and lack of important information, I really don't know for sure what these oils are.
Because of the deceptive practices and claims made, I would not recommend these or any of their other oils.

title: Deceptive, and cheap.
text:
I am so very disappointed with this product line by Amorepacific. I love their other brands, IOPE and sulwhasoo. But I was in the search for a more affordable toner/emulsion/serum and was excited when they introduced this line and gave a discount. They really sold this beta-hyaluronic whatever that works 1.5x better and I thought it was a new patented technology. But no. Contrary to their marketing claim, there is no such thing as beta hyaluronic acid. Yes I looked up patent registry and trademark registry and Amorepacific didn’t register anything new in the past few years related to hyaluronic acid. They just put a new spin on beta glucan, which according to some studies works 20% better, not 150% like they claim. Also beta glucan is toward the end of the ingredient list, meaning we have no idea how much of it is even in there. It’s so disappointing that Amorepacific decides to just flat out lie to customers about it. Makes me go wonder what else they are lying about.

Now I would not have done all the research if the serum worked well in the first place. But it came with no safety seal which made me go um. The packaging felt cheap. The liquid felt cheap and diluted. My skin smelled like plastic. My skin didn’t stay hydrated like other serums and that’s when I knew something was up. I bought toner, emulsion and serum. The emulsion was sealed but the toner and serum was not. I didn’t even bother trying the emulsion. I’ll be returning these all. I will also be seeking new skincare products that are not made by Amorepacific. Goodbye.

Vitamin A stimulates and thickens the dermis where collagen, blood vessels and elastin are thereby reducing wrinkles and increasing blood flow to the surface of your skin. Vitamin A actually expands the deposit of collagen in the skin; therefore slowing down the normal aging breakdown of your collagen and elastin. I've also read when studying skin care (and I really researched it) that Vitamin A increases blood flow and reduces the symptoms of rosacea, helps heal wounds more quickly, repairs cells in the skin and optimizes UV protection, exfoliates to make the skin more smooth, supple and even and even decreases melanin granules reducing brown spots and pigmentation. Skins miracle healer!My mother has always used vitamin E. She is in her 70's and still has beautiful skin and is very selective about what she puts on her skin. I've read that Vitamin E has been used in skincare for so long that it sometimes gets passed over for newer, more exotic-sounding ingredients that are sometimes advertised or added to products. It's good that the items come in a pump, because exposure to air effects good quality ingredients. A little goes a long way, and the product seems to be lasting a good long time. I use many of Majestic Pure products, and I have had excellent luck with them all and no issues. This moisturizer already is reducing fine line and wrinkles in my skin. It really helps to keep down oiliness and shine off my face. I use this moisturizer on clean skin and I let it soak in, and use under the the throat and jaw line for added firmness. While I am applying my eye makeup, I let the cream soak in. This anti aging skin cream keeps your skin supple and moisturized. title: VERY Small Bottle, But Works Well
text:
I have been looking for some shampoos to help with cleaning hair, but also making the scalp heal for nice hair growth and also flaking.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes wrapped tight in plastic with the pump down.

HOW TO USE
Once the plastic is open, you turn the pump to make it pop up and then you can dispense the shampoo.

SIZE
The bottle is only 6 inches from the base to the top of the pump. It is pretty small.

SCENT
My mom found a really old bottle of shampoo in her attic that was by Fabrege called Farrah Fawcett shampoo. This scent reminds me of that. It is a really nice smelling shampoo.

SCALP
I did feel some tingling in my scalp when using this. It did not burn or hurt at all, it felt nice.

HAIR CLEAN?
I have very fine hair which is easily weighed down. It is hard to find a shampoo that encourages volume, does not make my hair look flat, and that does not make it full of static. This shampoo leaves my hair clean for a few days and it somewhat encourages waves. I can not comment on static, as it is not near winter yet. My hair was not left dry or frizzy at all.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice shampoo. It is a small bottle, but a little bit goes a long way. It makes my scalp feel better and leaves my hair nice and clean.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish the bottle was not so small, but I do like the shampoo. I was going to give this to my daughter (she has scalp issues) but I think I will buy her a 2nd one and keep this one for me.

title: Great value gloves - lots of uses
text:
Great value gloves - lots of uses! I originally bought them to wear when I needed to go through old dusty papers that tended to make my hands dry and itchy. Lately though, I've taken advantage of having so many spares and cut off the fingertips so I could wear them while sewing or knitting. They keep my hands warm in my chilly house and are thin enough that they don't interfere with precise hand motions. I also use them while drawing and inking and they help keep my wrist from smudging on the paper.

Sizing/ Fit/ Material: I can usually wear Medium or Large latex gloves, and got these cotton gloves in Large. The fit is a bit loose in the palm of the hand and tighter around the fingers. The fingers are way too long, but I either cut off the fingertips or just leave the tips smushed a bit inside-out. Note that gloves are cotton/poly material, so they're quite stretchy, but don't don't have the soft "cottony" feel of pure cotton. I was able to "seal" the edges with a lighter where I cut them, and they melted like a champ. The stitching on the seams is a bit loose, but I haven't had any problems with it coming undone.

This warmer does heat up and maintains the chosen temperature. We tested the warming device with massage oil, and it does a credible job. A nice touch is a red light indicates the device is in the heating process to attain the selected temperature. It turns green, when it's at the selected temperature, giving a 'green light' to use the warmed material.
Overall, it's a competent warming device that seems a bit pricey. It does meet expectations, earning a 3.75 - 4 star rating.

Because I frequently shave far away from an a/c outlet, I needed the timer display to tell me to get ready for a charge. This feature is a must and helped make my decision easy, on which new model to buy.

Only way to get my feature was to go for the top-of-the-line 9190 XL Norelco model and make the 200 smacker investment. Thus far it has lived up to my expectations. Shaves about 40 percent quicker than the older versions and is extremely quiet !

On the dark side, I have also found a couple of minor shortcomings: First, the travel-carrying case is difficult to unlatch. The only time it opened easily is when it fell on the floor ! This unit should not have popped open at all. Second, although the timer display is large, certain numbers are not so easy to read. A number 8 looks a lot like a 3.

All things considered, it has been a worthwhile purchase for me and should provide years of reliable service. This one you will enjoy !

title: You made it to this point - just get it
text:
You got here 1 of 2 ways - you are either into cyberpunk aesthetics, or you were searching for a specific scent. I was trying to track down vanillas and citrus scents, and came across Proto Alchemy, and they instantly got my attention. I am a dude. I am not a lumberjack, and I am not a suave, dapper, 3 piece suit wearing gentleman either. But every freaking beard oil hammers one of those two stereotypes home. It's really hard to tell if any of these companies are actually genuine, or just some faceless sub-brand marking up some garbage because having a nice beard is cool.

So I can tell you these guys (actually just this guy I think) are legit. Matte finish packaging, commissioned art from legit artists, and even a little bit of world building just for a beard oil. I am a designer - little details are important to me and can often speak to the quality of the actual product. And in this case it does, this is some damn good beard oil.

The oils work well, providing light shaping and conditioning. The bottles dispense nicely - I like being able to easily tap out a couple drops which is all i need for a 3-4 inch beard. I've had similar droplet dispensers (I don't know what those are called) that were slower or didn't work as well.

I first bought Anti-Hero. I don't drink whiskey and don't smoke, but this smell is really something else. Sweet, vanilla & musk with something else special to it. It reminded me of the hotel elevator in Athens during my honeymoon, that was overwhelmed with some foreign, exotic cologne. That will help none of you, but regardless, I believe it will still be a scent that reminds you of something or somewhere, but you can't quite place it. It drove me crazy for a week before I figured it out, and that scent is something I have been trying to figure out for a good 7 years. It's unique, I love it, and I still can't explain it. I was finding excuses to use it more than I needed to, and quickly ordered the other 2 scents.

Botanist is awesome. It is so far beyond what I can explain - I've read reviews on plenty of colognes and then gave up when I realized even if I knew what those words people used meant, I'd still have no idea how it could smell. I can definitely buy into the botany idea behind this scent, there is an earthiness to it but it also leans sweet. Another scent I really haven't come across before.

Islander I was really hopeful for, but it smelled a little too generic cologney. Maybe it's the rum? My previous favorite beard oil was citrus + vanilla, and I think the vanilla really sells the other two proto-alchemy scents. I don't hate it, it's still wearable unlike some others I have had to get rid of immediately, but I won't reorder it - unlike Botany and Anti-Hero, which I am planning on stocking up on, right now. I'd hate for them to disappear forever.

If I ran any sort of men's store, barber shop, or just a place that sold cool doo-dads, I would absolutely stock these and most likely sell a ton. They smell great, they look super cool and premium, and they are unique. Sadly, I don't. If you do, try that out for me. Best I can do is give them as gifts for now (or just hoard them for myself).

title: I wanted to love these...
text:
I really did want to love these. I had to cut off a bunch of hair after a bleach accident, and I HATE having short hair, so I've been curling it just to make it a little less awful. I obviously don't want to use heat when I'm trying to nurse my hair back to health, so my only real option is sleeping in curlers. Foam rods make great curls, but they are horribly uncomfortable, and my hair is too slippery for rag curlers when it's this short. These looked like a happy medium.

These are pretty easy to use - they roll well, and the wires keep them in place pretty well. They are much, much more comfortable to sleep in than foam rods. I understand that they have to be squishy to be comfortable; however they are just too small! I tried them every night for two weeks, and I never got the curls I wanted. They almost always ended up much too tight, except when I tried rolling larger sections, which ended up really uneven - tight in places and barely curled in others. I'm going for a defined curl, not soft waves, but these were ridiculous.

I ended up removing the foam and replacing it with cut-up foam rods, which was a slight improvement over just the foam rods. I'm currently testing (second night) foam rods that are very big but made of super squishy, comfortable foam. If they don't work, I'll go back to the hybrid of these and fosm rods til I find something better, do they aren't totally worthless, but I wouldn't buy them again.

title: Don't waste your time or money!
text: Okay, so I bought the Luscious Raspberries, totally excited to get the deep red shown on the box. Well, I can honestly say it turned a bright fuchsia/pink color instead. I have long hair, and required two boxes. This stuff is extremely hard to work with and it took at least 2 hours of dying before I was finished (this didn't include the hour of dying my hair blonde the night before). I chose to not use the bleach included to keep my hair from being fried, but I fear it may have turned out worse and my hair would've been way past fixing. The consistency of the die is not even close to a regular hair dye kit, it is like jelly and you are not able to squirt a bunch on and just rub it in. My boyfriend had to keep squirting a glob into his hand and smudging it into my hair that way. Then once the color is on, it will not spread. It coats the outside hairs and leaves ones on the inside uncolored, therefore it is extremely hard because you have to touch every single hair with the color individually or you will have blotches and dark spots. Also, I would recommend not getting into the shower to rinse because it stains the entire tub - walls, shower curtain, EVERYTHING. Looks like mass murder in the shower. It also stains anything that it touches. I am okay with how my hair turned out, only because I can rock the pink. If you are going to be pissed that your hair doesn't match the box, especially after all the hassle and money, DO NOT PURCHASE THIS PRODUCT.

title: I.love.my.epilator
text:
So, I HATED shaving my legs and did not have the bank account/ patience that professional waxing requires. It was this burning hatred of hair and relative certainty that laser hair removal is nowhere in my immediate future that motivated me to look into epilation. Also I am kind of addicted to self-tanning and shaving and waxing totally ruins a great faux tan.

I bought this epilator.

After using it on my arms and thighs for about a week with minimal discomfort, I downed a couple shots of vodka and began to epilate my calves.OUCH.Even after hanging out in a steamy shower for a half hour AND using it IN the shower, this was SUPER painful. But I kept going...

The couple days of doing my calves was intense (cursing, screaming, alarming my husband with my obsessive mission to rip the hair out of my legs), and there's no way I could get everything in one sitting since I have zero tolerance for pain. Anyhow I am so glad that I didn't stop!!!!

10 months later, I epilate once per week for about 15 minutes while watching tv (I no longer need to use the "wet" mode unless I wait 2 weeks between uses, more hair=more pain). It would have been nice if someone had given me one of these when I was like 15...thinking about all the money&time I have wasted on shaving is depressing.

Pros:

*Price- this is a great deal for all the money and time you will save
*Wet/Dry function- if you don't handle pain well, this is the ONLY thing that will get you through the early days
*Rechargable- No cords, no batteries.
*Multifunction- you can use it as a shaver or trimmer if you're so inclined
*Regrowth is not scary- your hair will be finer and tapered at the end, not angry and spikey like shaved hair

Cons:

*If you are new to epilation, it's going to hurt (but only the first couple of times)
*Grip-In the shower I've dropped it before because the grip isn't rubberized
*It's difficult to be 100% smooth(but you won't care because the remaining hairs are so fine)

I've read people complain about the battery...I plug mine in for an hour every couple of uses and it's fine. Also ingrown hairs seems to be a recurring theme...this hasn't been an issue for me, and if you exfoliate regularly you should be fine.

Of course I totally recommend this epilator to all my friends and family. I think it's great for beginners or even for the more experienced epilator-user who doesn't wish to be stuck next to an outlet.

text:
[[VIDEOID:19bb6cb5b35b75de6cd429e3da29e779]] These gel polishes are gorgeous colors! I found things I liked and disliked about them.

What I liked:
1. The kit comes in a pack of 10 and the color variety is good. This is a lot of polishes for the price.
2. The colors look the same wet and dry *see video* as well as on the bottle swatch.
3. They have lasted very well for me and I work with my hands a lot as well as play guitar often with no pick. This will chip your nails quickly, but this hasn't happened yet.

What I disliked:
1. This kit does not come with a base or top coat.
2. I already have a few base and top coats hanging around the house and the first attempt I made using this polish I used a base and top coat that was not comparable. It would not dry even when under the UV light for quite some time. The second attempt I switched my base and top coat to another brand and it worked. They should really just include the base and top coats if this is a potential for customers. Just keep this in mind if you find the polish isn't drying the first attempt.

Given the pros and cons as long as you can find a compatible base and top coat you'll really like this product, if you want to avoid the frustration I'd suggest finding a kit that includes the base and top coats already.

title: Big, Bigger, and Biggest
text:
This is an interesting set of mascara. I have my own favorite brand mascara but I was looking to lower the cost of my makeup budget and these mascara set fit the bill.

It is interesting to see that the company packed those containers in a way from right to left: big, bigger, and biggest and you can tell which is which by the sizing of those tubes.

"Big", the teal tube, is for natural days when I need a soft oomph to my eyelashes and it fit the bill. Very nice and it held up well during long days.

"Bigger" ,the yellow tube, is for between natural to thicker lashes, not necessarily long but it is nice to get extra fluffy lashes for days I want to show off my blue eyes. It had good lasting power but it did flake a bit after a very long day.

"Biggest", the purple tube" is the bomb. It has fibers in solution making eyelashes lengthen and thicken and it really makes my blue eyes pop. It flaked off a bit at the end of the day due to fibers but it's very minor compared to making my eyes look big and gorgeous.

I can choose which mascara that I want without guessing due to its different sizing even though I could just read the names on the tube but they are rather confusing.

I really like the ease of these mascara and they're so easy to remove with makeup wipes. You can even get the mascara to last longer by using makeup setting spray.

Yup, I will purchase them in the future and my budget will be easier to manage.

title: HUGE WARNING: It Contains DMDM Hydantoin
text:
It contains DMDM Hydantoin. This is a cancer causing ingredient. I encourage you to read about DMDM Hydantoin. It is basically an unnecessary ingredient, which you will find in some shampoos, conditioners, body wash, lotions and other cosmetics. It is added as preservative (as if you need to preserve lotions/creams). It's not necessary to add to cosmetics; hence, not all brands use it. This ingredient turns into FORMALDEHYDE in liquids, which is classified as "known human carcinogen" by the IARC (International Agency for Research on Cancer).
I always check for this ingredient before I buy any cosmetics. Had I known it is used in this facial cream, I wouldn't have bought it. So the cream came out of the shipping package and went right into my trash. This was a waste of money.

title: I really wanted to LOVE this wig like some of the other reviewers
text:
I really wanted to LOVE this wig like some of the other reviewers, but I ran into some problems with it for my Halloween costume (Daenerys Targaryen). Don't get me wrong, it helpped me execute my costume wonderfully, but fell short in my opinion in three categories.
First, when I initially opened the wig, the fibers at the part/crown were for lack of better words bent in a strange way that could not be corrected, even with light heat from my flat iron (luckily for me this was a non-issue for my costume because I needed to pull the front pieces of hair back into braids, but re-wear is going to look a little strange). Second, because you are purchasing a light colored fiber wig that is woven on to a nude headpiece, some of your natural hair/the wig cap is bound to show through. My issue was that you could starkly see the edging of my nude wig cap through the wig. Lucky for me, I naturally have very light blonde hair, but I couldn't imagine what show through would look like with someone with dark hair (just something to keep in mind). Third, thank the lord I remembered my brush. This thing got crazy tangled, now I knew some would come because of the length I went with, but I was brushing at least once an hour to keep a "fresh look."
With all that being said, I would purchase this wig again (just hopefully ending up with one that has a better crown/part). It looks 10X better and more realistic than anything I could have picked up at a Halloween store for my costume, especially keeping cost in mind at $43.

title: Nice, But Time Consuming
text:
These are nice curlers and they are just as described, but I would say they are more suitable for teens and adults who tend to be more patient.
       My 10 year old daughter wanted to try them because she wanted curls without having to use a curling iron. She has somewhat thick hair so I got her two different sets with multiple size curlers so that we would definitely have enough and have the right size. Neither set included any instructions, but it's common sense to know that the hair needed to be wet prior and it was easy enough to figure out how to apply the curlers. However, neither of us realized how time consuming the whole process would be. Half way through applying the curlers, my daughter started to get antsy and didn't want to sit there anymore. She also said that it hurt a little when pulling the hair through some of the curlers. We managed to finish getting the curlers in her hair, but by the time we were finally done she was just over it all. She was no longer willing to even wait for her hair to dry. So within about 10 minute she had starting pulling all of the curlers back out. Which that was another process. You have to be careful pulling each one out because if you start doing it too fast the hair will get tangled and stuck in the curler.
     I still think these curlers are nice though and I do think they would have looked great if she would have waited long enough, but they just weren't for her. I would recommend them for someone who doesn't mind being patient for the end result. For my daughter though we learned that it's just better to use a more quicker / instant method to curl her hair.

title: Painful and kind of flawed
text:
Pros
• Sturdy and durable – The tweezers themselves are aluminum, but surprisingly sturdy.
• Great carrying case – Tweezers fit inside tube, just like a lipstick!
• Convenient mirror – Located inside of plastic tube that stores the tweezers.
• Easy to understand – Push a button and use.
• Light – Bright blue, useful in a way.
• Packaging – The packaging is honestly one of the best I’ve received a beauty product in. The bag is sheer with a ribbon in place for the draw string. It’s already filled with my other beauty products. The carrying case is what makes it though! It looks like a tube of lipstick, and when you remove the tweezers there’s a little mirror inside.
• Bellabe-esque spring wand – It works! It hurts like anything but man, it gets the job done. Beware areas with high density hair, it will nearly bring tears. Also, I didn’t find it effective on the outer lying hairs of my eyebrow, I believe the skin is too loose.

Cons
• Light – The button is flimsy and seems like it may break eventually. Also, when I attempted to turn the light off the first time I accidentally held down the button which actually made the light strobe. Also, it may seem silly but I felt like the light was a little too bright and washed out the area of my skin I was attacking. Finally, the light takes 3 of those watch like batteries, and I’m sorry to say that the odds of me taking time out of my day to go get these things once it dies are very slim. It does come with them included though, so for now that’s not an issue.
• Mirror – The mirror is definitely a convenience and the placement is a great idea, however, I feel like it would be more useful if the mirror was a magnifying one so I didn’t need to hold it so close to my face.
• Tweezers – The ends are not as slanted as I would like, and while I may be just tweezer challenged, I found myself chasing the same strand of hair for minutes at a time. It would be great if you could switch the tweezers that the light attaches to, but that doesn’t seem possible.

Overall, while the packaging for this product is awesome, I don’t think it’s for me. But hey, I could just be less tweezer savvy than others.

title: My go-to stampers
text:
These are the stamping plates that I use all the time. I stamp over gel nail polish with konad stamping polish, Essie polish, or Sallie Hanson insta-dri polish. When you first pull off the blue protective film, clean the plates really well with acetone. Then, I usually paint, scrape, roll, and then clean everything off without actually rolling the first stamping on my nails. I find the first stamping doesn't go well on a fresh plate, so I just don't waste my time.
After doing that, they stamp fine all the time. I have found at least one image in every stamper bundle that has stamping issues. I just don't use that stamp. These plates have intricate designs that transfer well. If you find that not all of your design is trasferring, first clean the plate really well with acetone. All that built-up dried polish affects the stamp. There are lots of good videos on stamping troubleshooting, too, if you are having trouble.
I stamp with a konad stamper, and scrape with an old credit card or empty gift cards. Metal scrapers will damage the plates.

title: Meh...
text:
I like false nails, but I don’t like really long ones. When I saw these looked short, I thought they’d be great! I wasn’t too sure about the diamond gemstones on them. I was a little worried they would look too gaudy, for my taste at least. But, the images of the nails on the hands in the product photos they didn’t look too bad, the ones on the thumbs seemed a little big but I figured that was okay.

So, I get them and see the diamond gemstones seem way bigger than they do in the product photos. But, I figure they’re worth a try anyways!

It took me FOREVER to sort them into their separate sizes. Of course, when I was laying them out to take the photos of them, I noticed that the plastic part you pull off the nail to reveal the adhesive have numbers on them 🤦‍♀️ Wish I would have seen them when I went to apply them! The instructions say NOTHING about them having numbered labels. And, the numbers are REALLY hard to see. So if you don’t have perfect eyesight, you might have a really hard time! I have perfect eyesight and still had trouble. I showed in a photo the best I could the number on one of the nails. That one is labeled 2. In the photo I have with them all separated and labeled, so maybe it will help someone avoid the headache of figuring it out!

The nails themselves I feel are kind of small and the thumbs I think are too big. Like my fingers aren’t too big. The 0 ones were too big for my thumbs. I had to go with the 1 ones. But then the 2 were too small for my middle finger. The 1 ones fit good, but there was only 3 of them and I was already going to use 2 of them for my thumbs. So I had to use the 0 ones for my thumbs which were too big, so they looked weird. I feel like only having 3 of each size isn’t enough. I wore these before taking the photo showing them all separated. I kept the ones I had worn and taken off to include them in their size group. Having only 3 of each size, if one size fits 2 different fingers, you’d need 4 so you wouldn’t have enough, which is an issue I had.

I don’t like that there’s only 2 sizes with nothing on them, both tiny, pinkie kind of size nails. Usually when I wear something - gems, designs, etc. on my nails, I either have the designs on my ring and pointer finger, just my ring finger, maybe my thumb as well. But not every finger. But with these you pretty much have to, except for your pinkie. The 2 sizes that have the other design on them (the 5 and 55 ones), those sizes are so darn close that it’s almost impossible to tell the difference. So it doesn’t give much choice to have those on different fingers either. I ended up putting them on my pointer finger. So every finger had a diamond gemstone except for the pointer fingers that had the other design and the pinkies that had nothing.

I like that the set comes with the stick for your cuticles, the nail file, and a alcohol swab. The nail file is great. The nails stick well. I used the cuticle stick to push back my cuticles, filed my nails, and then used the alcohol swab on them. Then I attached the nails. I used them as stick on ones, with the adhesive only. If you wanted them to last longer, you could use glue as well. I just wanted to test them out how they were so I only used the adhesive that’s on each nail. They stuck very well. The only issue I had was the size 1 ones that I used for my middle finger didn’t curve over my middle finger well, so the corner looked like it was sort of lifted. But it still stayed stuck on well and didn’t pop off throughout the 2 days I had them on, doing all the normal things I do every day. They probably would have lasted much longer, but I didn’t want them on anymore. I didn’t like how big the diamond gemstones were. I didn’t like they had the diamond gemstones on so many nails. As I said, I would have preferred only having them on the ring finger, maybe pointer finger, possibly thumb. But not all. I didn’t like the ones on my thumbs (the 0’s) looked so big since I had to use those on my thumbs instead of the 1’s since I had to use those on my middle fingers.

Overall, for $15.20 (at the time of writing this review), I don’t think they’re worth it at all. If you feel your fingers are the right size to have better options when choosing sizes, if you like bigger gemstones, if you like gemstones on pretty much every nail, then you would probably really enjoy these. Like I said, they apply well and stick well. But, if you’re like me and don’t like big gemstones on your nails and don’t like gemstones on pretty much every nail, then these probably aren’t for you. Honestly, I can get a set that has more size options and designs I really like at the drugstore for way less. So these just aren’t for me!

title: Damaged or do it yourself? Is it cruelty free....
text:
Feathers can be a little controversial. Rest assured that these are cruelty free! I used to have a peacock as a pet. He shed those beautiful tail feathers every year, and even though he is long gone I still have some of his gorgeous plumes. Peacock feathers are not harvested from the animal, you simply pick them up as they are naturally shed.
This set arrived in a plastic bag. When I pulled the pieces out, there were three peacock feather pieces and one headband. Each feather piece has a rhinestone accent at the bottom. One is all rhinestone, one is a pearl surrounded by rhinestones, and one is a London blue stone surrounded by rhinestones.
Of the two larger pieces, one has an alligator clip hot glued onto the felt backing, and one has a strip of grossgrain ribbon glued to the back. Although I'm not sure, I suspect that it was at one time glued to the headband, or they leave it to the consumer to glue it to the headband. I tried to push the end of the headband through the middle of the ribbon, thinking that perhaps it could slide on, but it is glued completely, you can't slide it onto the headband.
The smaller piece also has an alligator type clip of the same size as the larger clipped piece. They stay beautifully in your hair and are actually comfortable.

I wouldn't call this a glamor or fashion accessory set, it's definitely a costume set that would be great for a roaring twenties party. Each one would also be a fun addition to a hat. I wear a lot of hats and love to adorn them with scarves and feathers.

The following is not part of my review but it is a kind of funny peacock story. naturally, when guests came over they wanted to see him with his tail spread out in beautiful peacock glory. They only open up like that when they're trying to impress someone, and he certainly was never impressed by any of my guests. At the time I also had a miniature pig. That peacock was so in love with the pig that whenever she came near him he would spread out his feathers and shake them hoping she would notice and return his love. Of course that never happened, the pig could care less. But whenever we wanted to show him off to our friends, we would walk the pig over to him and he would immediately open his tail feathers with a great flourish! My friends and I were all impressed. Maggie the pig was not.

title: Very good with limitations
text:
I've owned this toothbrush for nearly a year now and have no problems. I do, however, recognize the limitations of the design. If you expect to be able to rinse off the handle or submerge this toothbrush, you will be one of the many disappointed reviewers. Now, I owned two previous sonicare toothbrushes and I was never really happy with the life of the internal batteries. This is the reason I decided to go with this unit and I have not regretted my decision. My 12 year old daughter has also had this toothbrush for almost a year now and NO problems. While I do believe there could be inconsistencies in quality control, I think one can work around these shortfalls.

Here's how I believe I've managed to keep my sonicare running.
1. I don't put the handle under water, only the part that goes in my mouth
2. I ALWAYS make sure to place a little vasoline on the O-Ring when I replace the batteries
3. I fling the water off the brush after I rinse the end off.
4. I don't leave the brush standing up. This prevents any residual water from running down the handle. I always leave the brush laying out flat/horizontal.

Now, I realize one shouldn't have to do all this stuff to keep the brush working properly but, for me, it's a small inconvenience considering I have the ability to change the batteries.

Bottom line. I really like my toothbrush but the design is not bullet proof.

title: Engineered to fail
text:
This product is good while it lasts; it'll clean your teeth better than almost anything out there (unless you have tartar, then you'll need something with a bit more power) and stimulate your gums. However, having autopsied this model, I am convinced that it was engineered to fail under typical conditions after a time, perhaps to motivate the purchase of a more expensive model, which will itself become useless when the irreplaceable batteries go out.

The first one I bought lasted a year, and even that long only after I learned that you have to plug the two holes in the back of the battery compartment to prevent the corrosion from taking place. By the end, batteries were lasting one week tops, at 2x use per day. I also learned that you have to hit it against hard objects when it won't turn on and sometimes then it'll go. You also need to scrape off any rust from the battery contacts occasionally.

Knowing these quirks, I bought another one and immediately plugged up the holes in the back and put tape around the battery cap. However, it has now lasted only a month. There's no rust or corrosion to speak of, however, it just doesn't turn on anymore.

Today I autopsied the first sonicare to see why it had failed (the new one is still on warranty). In taking it apart, it's clear that most of your money goes into buying a tank-like shell around the $1 worth of electronics. This would be a good thing, if there were not two gaping holes in the battery cap that let water in anyway and the shoddy rubber seal. After taking it apart, it's clear why the corrosion so quickly leads the failure. They protect everything on the circuit-board from corrosion by putting glue over it, except the battery contacts, and the contacts and wires that lead to the solenoid coil (that makes the brush vibrate). The contacts that lead to the solenoid and the battery contacts are also strategically located next to each other on the circuit board, so they can corrode together quickly using any moisture from the adjacent battery-terminal holes, while the non-essentials like the timer are located on the other side of the board and completely sealed off from the ambient air by glue. This also explains why hitting it sometimes allows it to start; you're shaking some of the corrosion loose.

The switch is also of questionable design, being nothing more than a paper-thin piece of plastic with some kind ring on it that's slightly more conductive than the plastic.

If the replacement that I get out of the warranty fails, I think I'll try a cybersonic or an oral-b; hopefully their teams of engineers weren't paid to make something less reliable than a politician.

Why can't they make a sonic toothbrush with no batteries, that plugs into the wall, and lasts a lifetime? Or just quit making these to fail so readily?

title: but I always hated feeling like I NEEDED to do my eyebrows before ...
text:
Honestly and truly, this eyebrow tint changed my life. I have naturally blonde hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes. I dye my hair regularly to a dark reddish brown, and obviously need my eyebrows and eyelashes to match so as not to look weird. I wear mascara everyday no problem and have been anyways for years, but I always hated feeling like I NEEDED to do my eyebrows before I went into public. Plus I hate feeling like they look drawn on and too done up. Beyond that, if I spent the night at anyone's house I would have to wear at least brow mascara to bed and risked looking bad when I woke up with it smeared all over my face.
I read the reviews before I used this and everyone said to leave the dye on for around 5 minutes. However the box says 2 minutes. The first time I used the dye I was freaking out a little because I thought I was messing up by leaving it on so long. DON'T WORRY. After the first time, I leave it on for closer to 10 minutes now. The dye definitely makes your brows dark, but that's what I prefer.
The first time I used this, it was before I went over to my boyfriend's house for the night. I literally was just laying in his bed smiling at how happy I was that I wasn't wearing any makeup, I felt confident in my brows looking good, and that I wouldn't have to worry about how I looked in the morning. It was such a great feeling! My eyebrows are one of my biggest insecurities and this gave me such a confidence boost!
I actually ended up opening all the little capsules and emptying them into the little bag provided and I just scoop out a little at a time to use. I did this because when I emptied an entire capsule into the little mixing pot, it made SO MUCH DYE and I ended up throwing away 3/4 of what I made. They give you 16 capsules but this still felt like a huge waste. This way I make smaller batches and have less waste and can stretch the product longer.
I'd say the only two cons of this product are that it only lasts maybe 5 days before I have to reapply, and that it's hard to apply it without staining your skin. So don't dye your eyebrows right before you leave your house, I try to do it at night and by the morning my natural oils have made the dye lift a little. By day two you can't see the stains anymore.

It accommodates my long hair and bow is just added for some degree of cuteness bc let's face it hard to feel the least bit attractive when wearing a shower cap. And contrary to another review I read the bow stays in place just fine - I can't fathom how hers didn't and sagged bc material is stiff. Only thing I will say it isn't as ample as picture leads you to believe. I understand we all have different sized heads, but it's shown to be extra poofy on pretty young model. Id share a picture of me wearing it but well that may scare people off and I do wish to leave a favorable review bc this cap actually does what it is meant to do - fit head and keep hair dry. End of story. Happy Bathing Ladies :)

title: Nice Cleanser That Leaves No Oily Residue, But Is Surprisingly Drying For My Skin
text:
This Neutrogena cleansing oil is nice and does a thorough job cleaning my face. The oil is initially applied with dry hands on your dry face, but you add water to your skin and that emulsifies the oil and makes it look and feel pretty much like soap. This cleanser leaves no residual oil on my face at all. In fact, it actually leaves my face a little dry as compared to my usual cleanser. Also, while it removes most of my mascara, I still need to use my Lancôme eye makeup remover to get rid of the last traces of non-waterproof mascara under my eyes.

This cleansing oil comes in a nice bottle with a pump that works well. It doesn't cause me any rash or irritation. This does have fragrance, but even though I can get headaches or allergic reactions to fragrance this one doesn't bother me. I think this is a nice cleansing oil that will work well for most skin types- except I wouldn't really recommend it if you have dry skin like me. And just keep in mind you may still need eye makeup remover. It's a nice product, except my skin is too dry to use it regularly. But it may be perfect for others. I give it 3.5 stars.

title: Meet my new best friend!
text:
OMFG this brush is amazing! I have 3B style curls and I'm also biracial so my hair is really porous and a bit on the fragile side. In its curly state it's a pain to care for but the traditional blow dry and flat iron method is both tedious and damaging to my hair.

When wet to straight irons came out, I immediately hopped on board because it just made more sense that heating my hair while wet would be less damaging to it. Through this I got hooked lol. But even with that it is a bit tedious.... though it did help me figure out that I could flat iron my hair dry and skip the blow dryer.

My boyfriend has one of these brushes and I tried it as a quick way to straighten my hair in the am. I was SUPER impressed! But it had some design flaws that made me seek my own, and landed me here.

From what I've seen comparing this brush to the more popular Rinfy and his brush, they've reallly improved upon the original design concepts. Most notably, the buttons are on the front of the handle and not the sides, down near the cord instead of anywhere up near the head. This along with the way they're shaped to be concaved makes it highly unlikely they'll be pressed by accident. But even if you do press them by accident, the device automatically locks them about 30s after the temperature is set. If you want to change the temp or turn it off after that, you need to click the power button twice to unlock them.

The teeth are not only steep enough to accommodate my thick hair, but there's also way more of them packed more densely together. This seems to make this brush MUCH quicker at straightening my hair, and it can also get it board straight. The other brushes have only gotten it as close as a little wave.

Since my hair is so thick, I also have to place my hand on the bristles while I pull the brush through so it gets all my hair in it. This is the only model I've tried which hasn't burned me even once while using it so far. The teeth are so densely packed that there is no way for a finger or the side of my hand to slip down past the safety portion of it.

Quick heating? Honestly I don't know why anyone tries to claim that.... I've never seen any heated hair product heat up quickly. My stove doesn't even heat up quickly. I hardly expect my straightening iron or brush to defy the laws of physics so I don't have to wait a few minutes for it to heat up. That's why I turn it on BEFORE I'm ready to use it. 😉

All joking aside though, this really is a fantastic brush. It even FEELS high quality. Nice weight, premium plastics, slick design. It will fit right in with other hair devices no matter how pricey they are.

title: 3 Pack (White/Slate/Lake blue) of the Niutop Watchband Style Band for Fitbit One
text:
This review is for the 3 Pack (White/Slate/Lake blue) of the Niutop Watchband Style Band for Fitbit One. I received a promotional discount on this item in exchange for providing a review. I have been using this item daily for a little over a month and wanted to share my experience.

First Impressions
* The items were exactly as pictured, the colors really bright and crisp.
* It took some work getting the FitBit One in and out of the band. It gets a little easier the more you use it. I do not view this as a problem as I know its not going to fall out.
* Was not easy to insert the fasteners on the one end of the band to the connectors on the other. This is still and issue, but again, I do not view this as a negative as I can trust that it will remain secure, but it can be a pain, easier with help, to fasten it.

Observations from wearing.
* The FitBit One was very secure in the band, never worried nor experienced it falling out, coming loose, etc.
* Once fastened securely the band never unsnapped by accident.
* After the first week or so I started to get a rash on my wrist. I switched it to the other wrist and experienced the same thing. I took off the band, removed the FitBit, then washed the band in soap and water. I wore it for several weeks after this, on the same wrist, and did not experience any issues.
* I was used to clipping my FitBit to my pocket or shirt, and do not normally wear a watch. I did not have any problem wearing it, was very comfortable and often forgot I even had it on. It did take some getting used to, remember to remove for a shower, and not getting it overly wet while washing my hands, but I got used to it very quickly.
* I did notice a few occasions that if I made exaggerated arm movements it would trigger as steps on my FitBit one.

Overall
I would recommend this for anyone looking for a watchband style carry for their FitBit. I use mine daily and I not even considered going back to clip style carry. I do recommend that when you first receive it that you wash it with soap and water, rinse and let dry before using. You will never need to worry about the FitBit becoming unsecured from the band.

title: fun colors, easy application with a little prep
text:
These are some fun colors from INH. They are not for the timid. I had used an INH semi-permanent color (pink quartz) before and knew what to expect. This time I tried Wish Bear that is a green blue color. I have curly hair and usually just add color to a few curls around my face, but this time I was feeling crazy and did a full head application. I had mixed results with the different levels of dark and light in my hair. I would say that the image with the different results based on your starting color are accurate. If you have a mix of levels in your hair then you will get a mixed look, too. This will look best (and get you that prettiest Care Bear color) on a pre bleached platinum level hair.

Application is easy if you prep you surfaces (old towels are great) and wear gloves during application. I followed the instructions and had washed the night before so I was applying to dry unconditioned hair. I didn't use a bowl and a brush. I just used my fingers and was careful to section and saturate. I left it on for an hour because I know from using semi-permanent colors over the last year that I need longer than the usual 30 minutes. On pastel shades I usually go an hour to two hours. If you are unsure then do a strand test before you go all over crazy like I did.

My hair felt great afterwards. It is conditioning. It very much reminds me of the expensive brand that starts with an O. Would I get this particular color again? For me, probably not. I did not have light enough hair to get the Care Bear look. I also don't think the green in the blue green works on me. Would I get this brand again? I sure would.

I do not understand the hype of Harry's razors. My first issue as an 'in the shower' shaver is that the grip is not that great. There are 5 blades, a moisture strip and some other strip that makes it a bulky head that feels like I'm dragging a razor paddle across my face. I find that it does not offer a very close shave and I have to go over spots numerous times and still I will sometimes realize later in the morning/day that I have a rough spot somewhere that was not cleanly shaved. Particularly along the jawline where my face is more curved and not so flat. The bulkiness of the razor head is also a nuisance for shaving mustache area, you can't get a close shave under your nose, you have to use the single blade detailer side which I don't care for using on the front of my face.

I do like their shave gel, it smells nice and makes for an otherwise smooth shaving experience. Not in this kit but so I can offer some other praise to Harry's is their peppermint face wash. I bought some of that too and have enjoyed it.

text:
I have no idea whether this product works, but that's only the part of the reason why I am giving this only 2 stars.

I'm an older guy who still has bad acne scars from my teens and 20s. The prospect of owning a product that might help make some of those scars less visible was appealing, thus I purchased it.

It came well-packaged - but with no instructions. Other than deodorant and cologne, some men might buy moisturizer, but most don't know facial products as well as women know theirs. I'd already received a "Did you receive our product?" email, and I decided to respond. I informed the vendor that I did receive the product - but knew nothing about how to apply it. I asked whether only a drop was needed and spread around, or if a greater amount should be applied. I asked about "How much should I apply - liberally, or just a small drop? ...Leave on the surface of the skin, or rub it in?
