title: No difference after three weeks of consistent use, and product won't dispense through pump.
text:
ANOTHER UPDATE:

My dermatologist told me that unless a Vitamin C serum contained the L-ascorbic acid form of Vitamin C, I was wasting my money and doing little to improve my skin. I found a serum here on Amazon that contains 17% L-ascorbic acid, and I've been using it for approx. 3 weeks. What a difference! I can definitely feel it working for one thing (it burns for about 5 seconds), but more importantly, I can SEE the difference in my skin already. At first I thought my eyesight was going downhill, but then I realized my skin really did look smoother and had a new glow. Do an Amazon search for L-ascorbic Vitamin C serum to get the good stuff.

Having said all this, I have added a LOT more spinach to my daily regimen lately, so I'm sure that's contributing to my skin's appearance too.

UPDATE:

I finished the bottle which gave me about 5 weeks of use. If it made any difference in my skin, it's at a microscopic level. I'm buying another bottle - mainly because there's got to be SOME truth to all the 5-star reviews. But if, after another month or so of use, I still don't see improvement in my skin, I'm asking a dermatologist for a Rx for Retin-A.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I've been using this product for three weeks, and I have yet to see any improvement in my skin. I'm amazed (and not a little skeptical) about some people seeing results in two weeks. I also wonder how many 5-star reviews were written by people who were given the product to try.

I'm very methodical about using new products on my skin. I use a 10x magnifying mirror, establish a "baseline" area of my skin to observe over time, and take close-up "selfies" of my skin to compare with photos taken a few weeks later. No difference so far, but I'll continue to use this product until it's gone.

I DO like that this retinol doesn't irritate my skin, which is highly unusual. So unusual, it makes me wonder if it indeed contains any retinol.

In conclusion, and not a critique of the product itself, but the product won't dispense through the pump. It's too thick. I'm having to pull the cap off and shake the serum on to my fingertips. I wish it came with a dropper instead. I changed out out the pump with a dropper from another bottle of serum. I'm surprised I haven't read about this problem in other reviews. Another reason I'm leery of all the glowing comments.

I'll update with my progress, or lack thereof, at a later date.

I bought the Panasonic because of the Linear motor. It also had the fastest motor speed. It doesn't get slower as the battery drains. I think the motor was actually too fast to get a great shave.

My old single blade Norelco (8894XL) is great. The motor seems too slow at first and the shave takes a little longer, but I liked the results and the way it looks and feels. It was time to replace the blades again, so I decided to go for newer technology.

title: Best electric shaver I've ever used
text:
This is the first rotary shaver I've owned, and it is by far the most comfortable shaver I've ever used. I have very curly whiskers, so they're essentially flat ribbons that tend to confound normally-shaped shavers and make it difficult for me to get a close shave when using a razor. With this shaver, I can go in a circular motion, much more easily catching the whiskers on any part of my face or neck. While I need to use a pre-shave (like Lectric Shave), I've needed that for every shaver I've used.

Cleaning is much easier with this one than any other I've used. Simply open the heads and rinse with hot water. I previously used a Braun Activator, which was self-cleaning but required special cleaning cartridges that cost anywhere from $8 - $12 for a 2-pack; over 4 years of use and regular cleaning, that brought the total cost of ownership of the unit to at least twice what I initially paid for it.

The only caveat with this shaver is the tiny trimmer; since I only use it for my sideburns it isn't a big deal for me. However, if you have a moustache and/or beard you need to trim, you might need a separate trimmer.

Overall I believe this is an excellent shaver for the price.

title: Love this USDA certified Castor oil!

If your use to the super tall 16oz plastic bottles of castor oil for a dirt cheap price, probably cheaper than this 4oz bottle, then your probably not understanding what is so great about castor oil. You more or less probably just use the castor oil as a cheap carrier oil to dilute essential oils, which I myself also do with those big cheap 16oz bottles. If your looking at this bottle and then the price and thinking no way, then I can guarantee you've never tried Pure, "real" ,no filler, Castor oil, because if you did, you would understand why this 4oz bottle costs what it does. Also you would have reaped the benefits in probably more ways than one from using True Castor oil , and would think this is actually a really great price for USDA organic certified castor oil. I use this oil as part of my night time facial regime, and it's also amazing at getting rid of scars and stretch marks.
This oil can also be used to help grow fuller darker lashes, eyebrows and you can even add it to your shampoo and or conditioner to improve the overall health and growth of your hair. The only Castor oil that I will put in my hair and on my face is USDA certified, otherwise you have no reassurance that what your using, especially on your face, is in fact pure and without fillers. Because of this not being a food item, the regulations on it are extremely light, and therefore companies can mix castor oil with water or other things and slap a pure castor oil label on it, and not have to disclose that it's been diluted in one way or any other. The ONLY way to know for sure is to purchase a bottle that's been stamped with the USDA stamp, which she means it has gone thru rigorous testing and is in fact pure with nothing added to it in anyway.
Pure castor oil is going to be semi thick, exactly like this oil from RejuveNaturals. This is great oil and I'm very satisfied with the purchase and recommend if you haven't tried pure USDA certified castor oil that you purchase a bottle of this castor oil from RejuveNaturals, it will change the way you look at castor oil forever. But the lashes themselves do not stay! the first time trying this product, I applied the eyeliner and let it dry. The lashes refused to actually "stick" (magnetic) to the liner and the lashes kept falling off. Thinking it was an error on my part, I attempted again, this time applying 2 layers (allowing to dry before the 2nd application) thinking I had not applied enough the first time. This seemed to help very slightly and the lashes would "attach" but only in random tiny spots, which was not enough to actually hold the lash in place. On top of this issue, I found that after wearing the liner for a few min., it started to "flake" and i kept finding tiny little black pieces in my eye. I wear contacts so this helped the pieces from scratching my actual eye, but it also showed me just how much was actually in my eye upon taking the contacts out. I watched some videos to ensure my issues were not simply user error, but it seems I was doing exactly as intended. I decided to go back to the magnetic lashes without the liner (2 lash strips basically "sandwich" your lashes between them while they "stick" together with magnets on each lash strip.)

title: Much easier to use than I thought it was going to be.
text:
At first I wasn't interested in an IPL because I had tried epilators and figured this was going to hurt. Then I read a few things on it and women were saying that it didn't hurt at all, in fact they said it was like blasts of ice cold air. So I decided to give it a try. Right out of the box I was impressed with the quality of this IPL hair remover. It is a solid unit and feels great in your hand! I love the overlay of gold accents contrasted by the neutral white color. The device is very aesthetically pleasing and looks like it could compete easily with the much more expensive ones. I do wish it came with a nice carrying bag or storage bag. But, I really can't criticize it for that because it is so reasonably priced!
Once you understand how to use this device, it is very simple to use. Getting to that place is rather hard because the instructions are not as clear as they could be and the print is super small. I went online and read up on how to use this machine before it ever got here, and I'm really glad that I did because it really helped me. I found out that are things you need to know before you ever order this unit, so you may want to check out some information online beforehand.
I didn't feel like it was an ice blast, you can feel the heat from this device while using it, so you know if you're going to burn yourself. In my opinion you would have to purposely have to ignore the pain to burn yourself because you feel the heat intensify as you leave it in one spot. This one only comes with one size head so it is a little tricky to use around your mouth area. It also came with sunglasses which I did end up using because the flashes were rather bright. They also don't recommend using an electric razor before because it can cause a rash, so they say to shave in the shower before hand.
I am very satisfied with this device and plan on using it about 3 times a week for the first few weeks, dropping down to 2 times a week for the next couple of weeks, and then down to 1 time until I don't notice the hair coming back in. Overall, I really like it more than I thought I would.

title: I have fallen in love with Artic Fox
text:
Wow, wow WOW! I have fallen in love with Artic Fox! I was so excited to try it, after seeing it demonstrated by a YouTuber I follow.

I tried Wrath on my own hair last week, so picked up an 8oz bottle of Violet Dream for my 20 year old daughter, who has bleached, waist-length hair. She did MP's Purple Haze two months ago and it did not hold long at all, which was disappointing.

We applied to damp, towel-dried hair and the 8oz was just enough. We put on a plastic cap and wrapped her hair in the towel. We left it on for two hours and it looks amazing!

Tips for those new to this type of haircolor...if your hair is not previously bleached, freshly bleached or very damaged, it's not going to give you the same intensity of the color you see on the box or in the pictures. So you might want to try a strand test if this is important to you. For instance, if you have dark blond hair and you put a green or green-ish blue over it, it's likely to look very muddy and grayish and not in a nice way. Cool colors especially work best on very lightened hair. Also, don't wash after rinsing out...just condition and then wait a couple days to wash if you can. Make sure to use a gentle, sulfate-free colors-afe shampoo. And skip shampoo often, and just rinse and condition (you can wash your scalp with conditioner). Also, "strip" your hair before applying...use a clarifying shampoo so remove any oils or build-up that will keep the color from getting info your hair! This is how I get my color to stay well for a couple months. :D

title: Great price, fantastic products
text:
I've been searching for the perfect liquid lip stain for years now, and all three products in this set (the ink velvet and the water tints) fit the bill. So many other products dry too quickly and have applicators that are either stick straight or a standard doefoot. Neither is great for poutier lips, and mine aren't even that pouty. Peripera managed to perfect the formula and applicator for me. The applicator is at a slight angle, which helps to follow the curves of your lips while still getting an even line along the edges. The formulas apply uniformly, and you get a bit of leeway before they set. They also don't enhance lip lines or dry out my lips (my biggest pet peeves with other liquid lip stains). I think the contour product is better as an overall bronzer than a contour because it's so sheer. The blush is a standard pink that should work for most skin tones.

My only complaint is that when you put in all the shelves, all five products will not fit in the fridge. I've tried various combos and can only get four of them in.

title: Very rich and moisturizing - thick cream
text:
This is an interesting face mask. You get 5 masks for $20 so an ok price, maybe slightly more expensive than usual. You apply this mask to a clean face like you always do. When you open the package you find 2 masks in it, they split the mask up into 2, the top and bottom.

This mask is the first cream mask I have ever used. You will first notice the pleasant scent, the reason I ordered this in the first place. I have a serum by Abib that I love and has an incredible fragrance so I figured this one has to be a great product. This mask feels kind of weird on your face because of the cream. It reminds me a bit of nivea cream to be honest, fragrance wise and thickness / consistency wise. So after the 20 minutes are up you take it off and realize there is still a lot of cream on your face. So you gently massage it into your skin. My face felt a bit sticky from all that extra cream to be honest. After about 20 minutes or so that feeling did start to fade, that is just how long it took for all of it to absorb. This is one rich cream I tell you. My face was nicely moisturized though and it definitely had a bit of a glow from all that cream to it to be honest.

All in all this is a nice mask, but maybe a bit too rich for me. I think this would do wonders when your skin is super dry, like on a horrible winter day when you have been outside in the wind all day and your skin is almost peeling off from the cold dry wind. This would restore it back to health. Right now my skin is just a bit too healthy I would say and this one would just be so much better when my skin is in dire need.

This beard balm has a flowery, feminine scent.  I can't smell cedar, sandalwood, musk, or leather in it.  I find it suspicious when a "natural" company doesn't list the names of the fragrance oils it uses in its product.  The scent ingredients on the can simply say "scented with premium grade essential OR fragrance oils."  "OR?" So which is it?  Fragrance oils are what people sell on the subway, and that's what this beard balm smells like: a generic, perfume-y scent.  You know when a product at, say, Rite Aid, says it's "mint eucalyptus" but when you get it home and smell it, it doesn't smell anything remotely like either of those things?  That's what the scent of this product reminded me of.  Flowery and feminine, no "old west" "leather" "outlaw" here.  If you want a feminine scent, get this product. title: One professional haircut LAST MARCH 2020
text:
As I write my review on August 7, it has been more than 5 months since I've been to a barber shop. The corona virus could do me in because I have a compromised immune system and I'm an old codger. I bought this cordless cutter thinking I could skip a trip to the barber and go half as often as I normally do, but this cutter has worked so well for me (with just a little help from my wife) that I might just go the entire year skipping the barber shop.

Despite having bursitis in both of my shoulders and arthritis everywhere, I'm able to "manipulate" and maneuver the cutter to give myself a "not too bad looking" haircut. The cutter comes with enough attachments that you can select the depth of the desired cut you need for different areas of hair needing trimming.

I'm impressed with how long the cutter can be turned on and used on a single charge, and the way the cutter is shaped, it is easy to hold. It pretty much conforms to my decrepit hands and is comfortable to hold.

If I were having to make a speech, or giving away a daughter at a wedding, I'd go to a professional barber for a "real" haircut, but for an "old codger" who often doesn't get off of the ranch much these days, this cutter does the job for cutting my own hair, during the "scare" of Covid-19.

The downside is that these polishes ship from overseas, so can take several weeks to arrive. They are well packaged and I did not have any breakage during shipment. In my opinion, these polishes are worth the wait and will save you a ton of money on expanding your gel polish selection.

UPDATE 9/2015:
After using these polishes for several months, there are a couple more things that I wanted to comment on.
The pros: I still believe that for the price, you won't find better gel polish. The durability is excellent and the colors are beautiful.
The cons: the colors don't match exactly with the photos so if you're trying to match a color based on the photo, you will likely be disappointed. The pigment saturation is generally lower than in more expensive polishes. Meaning, while some are good two coaters, others may need up to 4 or even 5 coats (especially the microglitters in set #022 which tend to have a more jelly formula).
My conclusion is still the same, however. I will continue to buy more sets of this polish as I grow my collection.

text:
Bought the pump for my elderly mother-in-law who has difficulty lifting the larger size mouthwash bottles and opening the caps. Works fine for our needs.

Pros:

Inexpensive solution - I paid $6.50 with free Prime shipping.

Cons:

Spout tip is angled outwards so place your cup directly underneath the tip to keep product in cup.

title: Works well. Be careful I thought the eyebrow razor was a shaper
text:
I got an electric Epilator awhile ago that I like a lot. It keeps you hair free for long periods of time and I've noticed the hair comes back thinner each time. I've used my electric Epilator everywhere but my eyebrows, for fear I might not have anyone I'm done. I saw this product and thought I'd give it a try to get the stray hairs and to do my eyebrows (hate wasting a Saturday morning to wax)

The directions on the back of the box are a bit vague. I was able to figure out how to maneuver the stainless steel coil and here's what I found.

I want to note at first glance I thought The free eyebrow raiser enclosed was an eyebrow brush to separate the hair. Thank God I have somewhat bushy eyebrows or they be gone 'd be gone! Now that I know how to use this razor I do really like it, I didn't want to knock off the star for my stupidity, it clearly states when I bought it it comes with an eyebrow razor. Just in case there is another woman tired coming home from work tired that wants to shape their eyebrows while cooking dinner, doing laundry and taking care of the kids .....there is a heads up '

I found by trial and error if you want to get the hairs between your eyebrows above your nose hold this horizontally and go side to side.

If you want to shape your eyebrow you can actually curve this below or above and gently move the coil around to get rid of strays.

If you have a single strand let's say on your chin you want to get I found that moving this down will grab that hair.

I was surprised at how much hair I took off with this thing

This does not hurt as much as the electric epilator does, I don't think the electric hurts that much either. When it gets to hear it hurts a little more than a wax and a lot less than a tattoo.

Once you get used to maneuvering this around it works great. It took me a couple days using this to be able to pinpoint to hear and I can now get it in about 20 seconds. It also does remove like here but it would take a long time to do.

This definitely works your wrist some, if you like the results I would say get an electric epilator and use this for your eyebrows and touchups. I have a little bit of carpal Tunnel, after about 15 minutes of twisting in moving this around it does get to my wrist a little bit, that being said I don't think this is meant for large area hair removal.

Hopefully my tips will save you some of the time I've spent experimenting with this. It's a neat little tool that I will definitely use. This may sound gross but I was actually able to even get a nose hair (if someone else is nervous to try it, I did, survived and like the results) lol

I did receive this product at a discount for my honest review. I thoroughly use any product before giving a review whether I get it for free at a discount or pay full price

title: Newer is not better
text:
Well, I've owned this razor for over a year now and I think I'm going back to my old Norelco 9160XL (similar to the current 8200 series). What don't I like about the Arcitec model?

1) It's loud--loud enough for my wife to complain in the morning when she is still trying to sleep. It is much louder than my 9160 which is nearly silent.
2) I don't think this new HQ10 blade set cuts as well as the HQ9 set. I believe I get a closer cut from the old razor, and with less effort. I find it easier to shave my neck with the 9160, which is exactly what I had hoped the Arcitec would do better, but it doesn't.
3) I don't like the hair trimmer design. The design on the 9160 (and current 8200) is much better. It's much more convenient to use and it trims better.
4) It's nearly double the price of the 8200 series.

What do I like about the Arcitec?

1) I like the design of the handle much better. It's thinner, longer, and feels better in your hand.
2) I can get about 1 month of daily use out of a single charge.

If it was quieter and it cut better I'd highly recommend it; but it doesn't. If I had to purchase a new razor today I'd buy the 8240. By the way, I've been using Norelco razors for decades. I've not had any problem whatsoever with my razors since they moved away from NiCad batteries (at least 5 years ago). The old razors batteries used to die and they were not replaceable, so you'd have to throw the whole thing away. But this is now very much a thing of the past. I highly recommend the brand.

title: Yes the Hair Grip Works
text:
I first saw this concept, Grip wrap for Wigs on Youtube. I searching on Amazon, I found many different makers, sellers.
I chose this one by the embroidered Logo (on the side) hoping for quality. They all resemble each other, quality didn't appear to be
the same, as you can find many of these for sale, names vary.

My (Brown) Hair Grip arrived today. I have tried it with two different Wigs.
1. Outre Dominican Blow Out Color #2 Half Wig with back and front combs and adjustable strap
2. FreeTress Equal Evyln lace front in Taffy. 2 side temple combs, back comb and adjustable strap

1. Outre: I did not need to use the front comb at all. I did apply the back comb, it's not necessary though.
I did it out of habit. The Half Wig is in it's natural place, snug, it's moveable yes, it's not going anywhere,
The Grip actually makes the wig look more natural upon my head, it pulls it inward as natural hair looks.

The Hair Grip wrap works as intended, no combs required to keep the wig in place, snug.

2. FreeTress Evyln Color Taffy. I did not use either side temple combs.
The Hair Grip I chose is dark brown.

Taffy Evyln is a dark root, darkest brown, blonde ombre,
if you really stare hard you can slightly see the grip/wrap in the part.
You would have to know it's there to detect it. I do not believe anyone would see it outright.

Again same result, The Hair Grip works as intended. The wig fit is snug, no way is it coming off.
Whatever the magic is with this The Hair Grip, it does enhance the actual fit of your wig in the positive.

I am glad I chose the Dark Brown Hair Grip vs the Beige, the Black, my natural hair is Darkest Brunette.
The brown color for me will be the most versatile for longevity of use and wear.

The actual fabric is very light, it's nearly weightless, it is not a velvet material.
The Velcro is soft to touch. I do not foresee it damaging my wig interiors, nor the hair either.

The Hair Grip is Firm " in place" there is not a feeling that I am wearing a headband..
No ring around the head feel. It's adjustable too, you can lighten or pull tighter, the velcro is ample.
The attach part of Velcro is about 2 inches, the connect side of the Velcro is several inches, this
will fit all heads, I can't see how it wouldnt.

Remember if you are wearing " wide' part lace fronts,
Color will come into play, the Grip is going to be visible depending on Wig color nearest the part.

I hope my review helps out, as it's a bit confusing with so many nearly same, yet not alike.

I am satisfied with my purchase, it is a worthy investment.

title: Patches Work Well...Not a Huge Fan of the Roller
text:
Somehow, I managed to dodge dark circles under my eyes for most of my life...until a few years ago. Now, they're the 'norm' for me. Same for puffy eyes. FRLEDM's 24K gold under eyes patches help tackle both issues and do so quickly. I keep the patches in the fridge-I get better results when they're cold and it feels good as well. I wear the patches in the morning for about 15 minutes and I'm good to go. It did take multiple uses before the results were obvious but that's to be expected. I like many of the ingredients in the patches, including: collagen, hyaluronic acid (HUGE fan!), and aloe, to name a few. I'm not a fan of the roller, unfortunately. I just do not care for the way it feels on skin...its not smooth and gentle, more like tugging and pulling. I will be passing it along to my mom who is anxious to try it.

While I'm not a fan of the roller, I am a fan of the patches and am pleased with the results they provide. I will continue to use the patches and definitely recommend them. I hate to say that I don't recommend the roller just because I don't like the way it feels so I will just say its not for me.

title: Nice Tea Tree blend lotion.  Fast absorbing, with good hydration and soft skin feeling.  Mild Tea Tree scent afterwards.
text:
I tried this recently on my dry knees and on my wife's dry itchy back. I used a bit on my knees, and it felt cool and moisturizing. I used quite a lot on my wife's entire back, and I could really smell the Tea Tree oil in this, that is without question. The product is a white lotion of normal consistency. I would not say it stands out in my mind as "breath taking" or anything like that. But, it is a well blended lotion with Tea Tree oil, as advertised. I have several bottles of Tea tree oil, and have used it for years, so I'm quite familiar with the scent and it's positive effects. This lotion is not runny, and holds together well as a large dollop on the back of my hand. It's texture is silky smooth during application, and it absorbs quickly, leaving a non-greasy feeling, with a moderate Tea Tree scent that lingers. When dried (less than 5 minutes), the skin is softer, and more hydrated feeling. This, like many "general blend" lotions containing a specific essential oil, gives you the short to medium term benefit of hydration and softness, with the nice smell and implied benefits of the oil it is blended with. This is not a high end night cream or eye cream, but a good quality hand, body, and face lotion in my opinion. Just as advertised. It's a good product.

But anyway...) I found it quit brilliant the way they gave us 2 smaller jars opposed to 1 larger jar. Smaller jar. (PS:  I keep My 2nd one in the fridge/ same with the 24k eye patches, but I’m going off subject again) You CAN keep your “open bottle” in the refrigerator- it’s a preference. Grime, gunk... so you don’t dry brush that. If you don’t wear any makeup.. then it’s up to you. I love My little face & neck dry brush. Up and outward. 8/10’light strokes. Then go on to your routine. Say bye bye to dead skin cells and your face received much more of the products you’re applying.  So Dry brush, Wash, Tone & Essence. And then I spot apply “Botulinum”... Once dry (if in. Hurry. title: Whoosh went the box
text:
This is a box containing a palette of 15 eye shadow colors, from a mustardy yellow (“ginger”), to a deep brown (“volcano”). Ingredients include: mica, magnesium stearate, dimethicone, bismuth oxychloride, capryly methicone, methylpaben, pro pylparaben, CI 77891, CI 77492, CI 77499, CI 77891. Each patch contains enough eye shadow for several applications, depending on how thick you like to go. Instructions say to apply with a brush or fingertip; no brush is included. The box has a magnetic closure, with a plastic sheet of transparent vinyl inside and comes in a cardboard sleeve. The product was made in China.

I have found this kit fun to experiment with. The colors are vibrant with a variety of earthy tones as well as some reds (“rose”). I tried using my own brush (no brush is supplied), but found I had better luck with my fingertips. The product stays put nicely without flaking and I haven’t noticed any skin reactions when I used it. I particularly like the darker brown colors like “bronze” or “ash”. For special occasions, some of the orangey/reds also look good like “pumpkin”. My biggest issue with this set is that when I first opened the box, it was cold and dry in my house, and as the magnets snapped open, some of the eye shadow patches spurted out of their pockets—I had “mermaid” spreading everywhere within the box. A brush would have been nice to include, but that probably would have raised the price, especially for a quality brush. Overall, this is a versatile eye shadow kit with attractive colors, but it doesn’t travel well. Best to use at home!

I take a cotton swab and add a drop from each bottle to the tip. I swirl the swab on the item to be tested and look for a pinkish color to appear, indicating nickel.

This is probably one of the best processing caps to get. Why? It pretty much fits your whole head unlike some others that are odd-shaped. Has very even heat compared to other caps - it is a bit cooler around the seams (which should be expected). I like the timer, don't have to sit and watch the clock and wonder "is that when I started?". 3 heat settings and I've used it on high with no problem when using with Malibu Crystal Gel Treatment.

The only thing I'd change is the strap. It's a bit 'hard' to get the strap through then through again the loops to tighten the strap under your chin and it doesn't stay tight tight. Thinking velcro maybe? So you could put the cap on and velcro the strap as tight or loose as you like. Otherwise, this cap has really come in handy. Both for deep oil conditioning treatments and when doing crystal gel demineralization treatments. Here's hoping this cap lasts!

I was acutally hired to test this along with two other rotary models and 5 other electric straight edges (remington-like) in a recent product test. All of us in the test group came back with the overwhelming nod toward the Spectra in every category -- comfort, closeness and easy of use.

The 'extra' features didn't matter much to me when I started, but my opinion quickly changed. Have a 'minutes remaining' to recharge was very useful when travelling. I knew whether I needed to bring the cord or not. That it is water resistant meant a little less worry when working near the wet sink. (I've also had this strange anxiety about it accidentally kerplunking into the toilet...now that fear is gone.)
There are not too many devices I use everyday, and that's how I'd justify the price. My cheaper norelco has been with me for about 5 years and I expect at least the same for this guy, so it can be amortized to about 10 cents a day.
I have tried and compared it to the others. Truly the best one out there, and I think you'd sacrifice a great deal taking a step down in price.

I was looking for a good serum to help my face look good for my upcoming wedding. I am a little older than my fiance but I didn't want my face to show it on my special day. The serum comes in a screw top and eye dropper dispenser. The bottle is a dark amber colored glass bottle. There is one fluid ounce in the bottle. The serum has a sort of medicinal scent, not unpleasant and not too strong. It leave behind no real scent once it absorbs in. The serum feels refreshing and absorbs quickly and thoroughly into my skin. I feel an immediate pleasant tightening effect and the skin looks smooth and supple almost immediately. I've been using the stone crop serum for two weeks which is not really enough time to be able to tell the full effect of the serum on fine lines and wrinkles, but I do notice softening in expression lines in my forehead and in fine lines and that my skin stays better hydrated throughout the day. There is no burning, redness or irritation with the use of the serum and no product residue left behind. The manufacturer offers a 100% Money-Back Guarantee which I appreciate but have never had a problem with Eva Naturals products before. I am enjoying the serum and consider it a good value at under 19.00 delivered to my door and by the fact that a little goes a long way with only one dropper full of serum enough to do my entire face.

title: It will leave your skin feeling soft and hydrated... down fall is how long they instruct you to leave on skin before rinsing.
text:
I have sensitive skin. I also have these small bumps where my body hair is coming through my skin's surface. The bumps are only bothersome because of appearance. I have a hard time using exfoliators because they end up irritating my skin. I love the properties that Coconuts possess and that is why I decided I would give Baebody's scrub a try.

This scrub has a very pleasant smell of coconut and almond. It has a similar texture to sugar, although the scrub has a wet feel to it because of the oils that are in it. The directions say to apply to clean damp skin. So obviously you would want to do this in the shower for a whole body scrub. The downside, and the reason for giving a 4 star and not 5 is that once you have massaged the scrub onto your skin you are then instructed to let the scrub sit until it dries (5-10 minutes). This is a time frame that really can not be utilized to shave your legs, or be done while conditioning your hair, you get to just stand there being cold. Also, I am a mother of a 2 year old boy... I am lucky to get 5-10 minutes to shower! It is difficult for me to use this product as directed in order to get the maximum benefits; however, there have been a couple occasions that I have been able to take my time in the shower and wait the 5-10 minutes. The way your skin feels on the surface isn't changed much by waiting out the time, If you use the scrub your skin is left feeling soft and hydrated. If you are able to wait the directed amount of time it will be worth it. Not only will your skin feel soft and hydrated, but if you let your skin really absorb the oils in the scrub then your skin is going to feel amazing for 4 or 5 days. If I am going to be applying the scrub I don't bother using my body wash. Instead I just use some shampoo to get my body clean because your going to be exfoliating anyways and the scrub has all the moisturizing power you need.

I use this scrub about once every 10 days or whenever my skin is really starting to feel "thirsty." I paid $1.95 to purchase this Baebody body scrub due to a discount that I received so that I could use it as I would normally in my everyday life and develop an honest opinion about it. I then take the time to leave a review detailing that opinion on Amazon in order to help shoppers know more about the product. I feel that it is very important to be honest and unbiased when leaving a review because it can have an impact on the decisions people make. I too rely on reviews that other post on Amazon when I am looking into products that I am considering purchasing even if I don't intend on buying the product on Amazon. There is no better feedback than that from actual customers and that is why I participate in reviewing products. The Baebody scrub will leave your skin feeling amazing, for how long depends on how long you are willing to let it dry before washing it off.

title: Hair is lovely and reverts back after washing it!
text:
I was pleased that her hair reverted back after I washed it. It's great to finally see more and more cosmetology mannequins with African textured hair that actually reverts back to its coily texture after you wash it. So often in the past, sellers would advertise cosmetology mannequins as having afro hair, then you washed it and the coil pattern was completely gone. The money I lost trying to find a real African textured cosmetology mannequin back in the day, was unbelievable!

A few things to note.....While washing her hair there was tons of shedding. I've come to realize this is quite normal. However, after the washing is said and done, the shedding is minimal. Thank goodness because there are cosmetology mannequins where the shedding continues in massive balls even after washing.

The ends are thin and stringy and that's where I'll take a one star deduction. She'll be gettin a good trim here soon, but I definitely recommend her. I'd say her hair is in the 3b/3c range? I could be off about that because I'm still a bit shaky on the hair typing system. Either way, you'll definitely be satisfied with your purchase.

I've attached pictures of before washing her hair, after washing her hair and what her hair looks like after I dried it and dry combed it. Lovely soft hair. I almost didn't wanna ruin the rod set because it was so cute but I always wash the hair of any cosmetology mannequin I buy, right outta the box.

title: All the strength of traditional arylic without the bulk or salon. Stronger and easier DIY then gel
text:
I have always coveted long nails, but with weak, bendy nails that peal and break easily it was never achievable. I'm a DIY girl when it comes to nails. I have been doing my own gel manicures for years and most recently have been using Brisa lite smoothing gel for added strength. It helped but manicures still started chipping at the 10 day mark and as soon as my nails got to the desired length they would start breaking.
By comparison this stuff is amazing! Its all the strength without the bulk of regular acrylic. They are my real nails but nothing will break them.The process itself is faster since you don't have to cure for two minutes each time. The coats between and after powder are just thin glue. Its also more forgiving as the coats are all even and solidly applied. You buff and clean up in the middle of the process which makes everything even and your edges perfect. I've also filed and such after they are done without issue.
I actually ordered from Revel itself, but read the reviews here first. Revel colors are also cheaper then gel's options, with a one ounce jar of color only costing about $8. One ounce jar is probably like 8-10 manicures. Sure beats paying a salon $40 every two weeks.
Removal is slightly different. I use the cotton ball with nail caps method and find it slightly more time consuming then gel, but I think that's only because I'm still getting used to it. When exposed to acetone the dip turns into a chewed gum consistency. So unlike my CND shellac that peals off I'm rubbing off sticky blobs. But I also probably just need to try soaking it an extra 5 minutes and stop being impatient.
But the extra removal time is totally worth it when you consider the manicures last longer, are stronger, and allow me to finally have my dream long nails.

title: Great product, better value
text:
TL;DR - It's cheap and it works.

Actual review:

I have been using Beardsmen Beard Oil for about 4 or 5 months now. There were 3 key factors and things I wanted to achieve in a beard oil (I had never used it previously):

1. I wanted it to stop the itching.
2. I wanted it to soften the hair for less of a "coarse" feeling.
3. I didn't want to spend $15 for 1 ounce of oil.

This bear oil hits all 3 points. Anyone who's shopped beard oils at all already knows it's probably the best value by far, you get 4x as much as what most other companies give you for the same price.

As for the itching, it definitely helps with that. You do have to make sure to rub the oil deep into the beard so it gets to your skin (Beardsmen gives you a link to a very detailed PDF guide on beard care and product use). If you just put the oil on the hair, it's not going to help your itchy skin (this is true for any oil).

Finally, beard softness. One quick anecdote will answer this: About a month ago I got lazy with my morning routine and stopped using beard oil (along with other things like face wash and cologne). About a week into this, I had some contact with my ex-wife (don't ask) and she specifically asked if I was still using the oil, as my beard was not as soft as it had been. When the ladies notice that you stopped using it, you know it works.

Long story short, I would easily consider this the "best buy" in beard oil.

title: Grainy but perfectly fine to use
text:
This shea butter is a good quality shea butter. It is ivory and reasonably priced. As a person whose been using shea butter for well over 10 years for ecezma treatment I can say that this shea butter is a quality product. Although it is a quality shea butter, the way it has been processed left the butter very grainy and not as creamy as I was expecting. It is a thick, heavy butter that is solid at room temperature and has a lot of use for hair and body purposes. It is sourced from an area in Africa that doesn't produce a real rancid smelling butter. It smells distinctly like shea but not like the shea sourced from more eastern countries. The butter when applied to the skin feels thick and heavey but that isn't a problem for me. I would need to indirectly melt and re-solidify this butter in order to smooth it out and kill the grainy texture it comes with. I'd also whip this butter to make it creamy.

Price: Reasonable
Texture: Grainy but not too smooth, sort of like peanut butter but thicker
Color: Ivory, more of an off white, cream like tone
Scent: Hard to describe but it's distinctly Shea which never smells pleasing

Overall, this company's shea butter is a good quality butter, high quality for some but for me good/decent due to the fact it's grainy and doesn't have the smooth texture I'm used too. The color is normal and the butter feels thick, heavy and heavenly on thick dry skin like eczema. I'd recommend this company's shea butter and possibly repurchase in the future.

•This quality shea butter was purchased for a promotional price in exchange for my unbiased and honest review.

title: Electrolysis... FOR WHENEVER YOU NEED IT
text:
Love being able to access electrolysis at home! I have been going to a professional for months now and when the 2020 pandemic began and all service providers closed up shop, I wasn't sure how I would deal with unwanted facial hair. Where other methods of hair removal can encourage stronger hair regrowth I did not want to regress. Then I found this! I have had this product several weeks now and am very happy with it. I wish I had found this earlier. Not only can I do a treatment whenever I want, I am able to target hairs when they first appear as opposed to waiting for an appointment. It is very easy to use. I was afraid I would be unable to target the follicle in the right spot but that has not been a problem. It has a high pitch buzz when the current is delivered to the follicle. Most of the time the sound is my only indication that anything is happening. I do not find this painful. I can tell it is working because when I go to remove the hair it comes out with no effort. I do keep the power at the highest setting except for the delicate area above the upper lip. That can be a painful area at home or at the salon.

My only complaint with the product is that the tweezers included are useless. Just use your own.
I bent the stylist at first so I did order extras to have in case that happens again... so far so good as I haven't ruined another. I don't think that is a product flaw as it must be very delicate to do the job right... just be careful.

If you are unfamiliar with electrolysis, do not expect that one shot will forever kill a hair. I suggest reading articles on the subject as this can be a long term process. But considering other methods are a FOREVER process... go for it !

title: The Real "Miracle In A Jar" For Me!
text:
I've been a user of the Alpha Hydrox products for several years. I'm 38 going on 39, and some people still mistake me for 25 to early 30's. I especially love the 12% Souffle cream. Trust me, if you purchase this product, it will work SO well that you may take it for granted someday. Don't! I made that mistake, and it almost cost me my skin!

I had run out of the souffle and was lazy one day when repurchasing my skin care products, so I bought a drugstore brand of a popular new "Simply Radiant" skin care system with fancy "Soy Proteins" in it. I wanted to even out my skin tone (African-American, with a couple of dark dots left over from a few small pimples). After using the moisturizer for a week, I started developing cystic acne-type bumps on my face!! BIG pus-filled lumps that developed in clusters on my cheeks and forehead. I was horrified. I immediately stopped using the moisturizer, and the cysts stopped developing, but the damage was done; I had slowly-healing cystic acne bumps on my face. When I returned the cream to the drug store, the clerk took one look at me and quickly gave me my money back; the bad skin reaction was that obvious.

I ordered the Alpha Hydrox 12% Souffle as soon as I could, along with the Alpha Hydrox 14% AHA swipes to help accelerate my skin exfoliation. I used the swipes 3 times a week, and the souffle morning and night. After a month, I finally got the acne under control. After two months, my skin was smooth again. After six months, I was able to take the most gorgeous headshots I've ever had done, and the graphic artist only had to retouch "shine" on my forehead and chin. There's only a pinhead-sized indentation left over from the acne scars, and all the deep-colored hyperpigmented spots have completely healed and disappeared. My skin is baby-smooth, even toned, and if I had told you that approximately eight months ago I had deep acne scars on my face, you would never believe me.

I'm back to just the Souffle morning and evening for maintenance, but I'll NEVER take using my Alpha Hydrox products for granted ever again!

title: Lightweight, Easy to Use Facial Brush with 2 Speeds and Pulsing Action
text:
I have used a Clarisonic Mia brush for more than two years, and although I like it, I've read that the Clarisonic brush can be too harsh. So, I was interested to try the Philips PureRadiance brush. First, the differences:

1. The Philips PureRadiance brush has two speeds, one is gentle and the other is a more intense option. This is a good feature, as in the winter when my skin is dry, a gentler speed is better for my skin.
2. The Philips PureRadiance brush has rotating bristles plus an pulsing feeling. The brush head is smaller than Clarisonic, so it is easy to use in small areas such as between your nose and mouth.
3. Similar to the Philips toothbrush, the PureRadiance brush has three timed sessions of 20 seconds each for three zones of your face. This is beneficial if you have a tendency to over scrub or irritate your skin.
4. The PureRadiance brush is smaller and lighter than the Clarisonic.

The PureRadiance is a different experience from the Clarisonic. It's not bad, just different. If this is your first facial brush, I think you will like the PureRadiance quite a bit. If you currently use a different brush, you'll need to compare features. If a gentle, light, easy to use brush is what you want, the Philips PureRadiance is a nice choice.

title: Second Ingredient is Mineral Oil/Paraffin

I purchased this item after reading the seller's description that lists a host of what I consider "good" ingredients. If you are opposed to using mineral oil (paraffin) in your hair, this is not the product for you. I contacted the company and was told that the paraffin is "approved per norms of ISI & British Pharmacopia/Indian Pharmacopia." My issue is not whether it is approved or not, but as the second ingredient, it should be listed in the description. If using mineral oil is not an issue for you, you may like this oil.

As for the effectiveness of the product, I did not use it. My rating is based solely on the ingredients. As one who is attempting to use more wholesome products, I found the omission of an ingredient that constitutes such a large portion of the entire product to be deceptive advertising. Rather than incur shipping costs to return this item, I threw it in the trash.

title: Cleans without clogging or over-drying
text:
I've used a number of cleansers since the late 80's due to somewhat permanent acne concerns. My skin seems to go between oily and dry, but a perfect balance is hard to find. The number one problem I've had with pretty much every cleanser I've ever used is that it either doesn't clean well enough, or else it cleans to the point that I have overly dry skin. Another problem that comes with cleansers that do clean well, is that after using them for a couple weeks, my skin adjust to the new chemistry and begins getting just as bad as before. If I miss a day of using the cleanser, then my skin gets even worse than it was before. Oh, and one more nice point, the cleanser is dense enough to only require a small amount at a time to clean your face, thus a single tube last a longer than expected.

With this cleanser my skin is better than its ever been, and despite 6 months of use, my skin still responds well to using it. Secondly, if I get lazy for a day and just use water on my face, I don't end up with any worse skin conditions. I highly recommend this, especially to those that have adult acne and have had a hard time find a cleanser that is worth the money.

text: I bought these at the recommendation of a friend and I LOVE THEM! For background, I am very low maintenance makeup-wise and have pretty minimal knowledge. They were insanely easy to put on, practically foolproof. The attached before/after photo is literally no makeup whatsoever, nothing except the eyeliner + lashes. Such a dramatic difference! I didn't have anything going on so I left them on all day just to test them out and see how durable they are. I took a nap in these. I wore them for 10+ hours before they started to detach a bit on the inside corners. I'm so impressed they lasted this well with no prep at all. To increase wear I recommend adding a primer first before putting on the eyeliner. Also the included instructions say to attach the lashes while the eyeliner is still wet but I think it works better if you let it dry first. I love how easy these are to use and I think the different sizes are great for different occasions. (The ones pictured were mid-size, there were longer and shorter ones in the pack).

text:
Although I didn't purchase this kit on Amazon, I'm writing this review so that others who are looking up reviews on this product will have a point of reference. Just for reference I have medium length, thin, straight, fine brown hair. I wasn't working with any kind of strange textures (coarse, thick, unruly, curly, crimped, etc) that typically would grab on to rollers.

title: Not sure what all the fuss is about...
text:
I will be the first to admit I hate taking baths; it bores me out of my skull. But because I have chronic pain, I've occasionally taken Epsom salt baths or bubble baths with a fantastic product called Muscle Soak. I found the salts were no longer really helping, so I thought I'd try these magnesium flakes. I take magnesium daily but a boost through the muscles that ache sounds great.

I was floored at how quickly and completely they dissolved. The tub wasn't done filling and they were fully absorbed into the water. With salts, I have to get in and stir repeatedly to get the crystals to dissolve, often in water that's hotter than comfortable. So that was promising.

I got in the tub and lay back, focused on the flower print on the wall....and was ready to get out in 15 minutes, but I wanted to give it the full 30. I wasn't magically relaxed or calmed by the bath as other reviewers are claiming. (You literally can't tell the flakes are there, as the water isn't salty like it is with Epsom salts.) I wasn't whisked away to a lush garden in my mind. I was just lying in a bathtub with pleasantly hot/warm water. While I was in the water and for up to an hour after I got out and showered, I felt a limited, temporary reduction in the tightness in my upper back. I put on a compression shirt to help things along but had 9/10 pain. When I can next score some Muscle Soak, I'll be going back to that. The bubbles are at least something to play with! And it is more effective on achy muscles.

This is not a magic cure for stress or pain. I'll use it to soak my feet when they ache, but don't expect miracles. If Epsom salts don't make a big difference, these flakes probably won't either.

title: Great for traveling
text:
I ordered this because I have a couple teeth that food gets stuck in a LOT and it's super annoying. I was using those picks but not only are they expensive BUT I noticed some of the plastic on it would be gone after using it on my teeth. Where was the plastic going? It was there and now it's not so it must be in my mouth! We do NOT need to be swallowing any more plastic!! I have a regular water pick and tooth brush combo but saw this and thought it would be GREAT travel with! Comes with a nice little bag to put it in which is nice because once you put water in it, unless you take it apart, there will be some water left in there. I squirt out as much as I can when I'm done but it's not totally cleaned out. That being said I think it's probably wise after a couple of months at least if not sooner you should maybe run some vinegar through it to clean it really well. I did that to start with to clean it before I used it.

As for the settings.... I would like if there were more than 3 but for a travel one I'm OK with it only being 3. As another reviewer said, you DO need to make sure the light is lit on the setting you want to start off with. I'm used to using a water pick so I like it up pretty high but you may not! If you're new start low.
I can get through all of my teeth in my water tank but I have to go fast. If I've had some sticky stuff I may have to fill it back up again for a second go round. I saw some bigger ones but I like how this one is a little smaller. It does it's job.
I don't have a problem with cleaning mine after each go round. Someone mentioned cleaning it after each time. I just wipe it off with my hand towel. It's water that came out of my mouth. I have my own hand towel that no one else uses and it's my spit and I wash my hands afterwards so I don't feel it needs to be sanitized all the time. Maybe if you were sharing it but this is mine!

I really like how you can charge it in any USB adapter. Super convenient these days.

It comes with several pieces. For the normal water picker to blow stuff from your teeth then there's plenty for others in the family or if you just want to use another while one is drying from being cleaned or something. I haven't used the tongue piece yet. I have a tongue scraper I'm fond of so this doesn't appeal to me.
I do really recommend this!

title: It actually does something.
text:
So, essences have always been a bit of a mystery to me (and, honestly, seemed like hokum) but my curiosity always led me back to research them. I've even bought them over the years and abandoned them because I just didn't know how to use them or if they were working. (And these are other best sellers with high price tags.) I finally revisited essences, caved in, and bought this super seller just to see if there was a fuss to be made over it. There is.

The very first time I applied it, I had a minor healing blemish on my cheekbone and it tingled at that spot. (Cool, it's not just water, lol.) I applied all my other stuff and knew it at least imparted moisture - my skin felt supple and hydrated. I noticed a change after just about a week using this - my skin was more even, a bit smoother (I have roughness on my cheeks that never seems to go away, no matter what), and dewy. I went camping for a few days - the dirty kind - and, after neglecting it, my skin needed help. I noticed everything bounced back much faster than it ordinarily would. I typically get a breakout after a trip like that but my skin stayed clear, it was just rough and sallow. Once home and finished with my usual routine, everything was back to normal and radiant again.

I know there are conflicting thoughts on how best to apply it; I won't put it on a cotton pad as I feel that would just waste too much product. (I first used this on May 6th and the picture is from 3 days ago - that's ALL I've used in about a month.) Right now I'm using one little drip of product for my whole face and neck; I just pour it in my hand, pat my hands together, and apply to a slightly damp face after toner. I must be experiencing what people are describing as a "water burst," because I put that tiny amount on my face and it's like I'm splashing water from a running faucet, that's the only way I can think to describe it; like the amount of wetness I'm getting exceeds the amount of product I used. I'm going to put some in a spray bottle with a fine-mist nozzle and use it that way, which is also how I'm going to travel with it. (Though, I've traveled with this large bottle and it's never leaked - and it lays on its side in my bag.)

For the price and the small amount I use, I will absolutely be repurchasing this.
(For reference, my once very-oily skin became dry then combo over this last winter, and now it's back to moderately oily, so it runs the gamut. I also have some unevenness, roughness on my cheeks, and dullness - all of which are improving everyday, and even my one or two monthly hormonal blemishes have been minimal and, if I get any small breakout, it's gone in a day or two and never fully forms to begin with.)
